rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall prepare all progress payment requests using RMS and shall update the work completed under the contract at least monthly, measured as percent or as specific quantities.
rows.normalized: Contractor must prepare payment requests using RMS and update work completed at least monthly.

rows.verbatim: After the update, the Contractor shall generate a payment request and prompt payment certification using RMS.
rows.normalized: Contractor must generate a payment request and prompt payment certification using RMS after the update.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall submit the signed prompt payment certification and payment request as well as supporting data either electronically or by hard copy.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit the signed certification, payment request, and supporting data electronically or by hard copy.

rows.verbatim: Unless waived by the Contracting Officer, a signed paper copy of the approved payment certification and request is also required and will govern in the event of discrepancy with the electronic version.
rows.normalized: Unless waived by the CO, Contractor must provide a signed paper copy of the approved payment certification/request, which governs over the electronic version.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall identify in his/her Quality Control Plan persons assigned as CQC System Manager and Alternate CQC System Manager.
rows.normalized: Contractor must identify CQC System Manager and Alternate in its QC Plan.

rows.verbatim:
These
individuals, within the onsite work organization, shall be responsible for
SECTION 01 45 00.15 10 Page 4 overall management of CQC and have the authority to act in all CQC matters for the Contractor.
rows.normalized: The CQC System Manager and Alternate must be responsible for overall CQC management and have authority to act in all CQC matters for the Contractor.

rows.verbatim:
The CQC System Manager shall be a construction person
with a minimum of 3 years (full time) experience in related equivalent
work.
rows.normalized: CQC System Manager must have a minimum of 3 years full-time related construction experience.

rows.verbatim:
This CQC System Manager shall be onsite at all times during
construction and shall be employed by the prime contractor.
rows.normalized: CQC System Manager must be onsite at all times during construction and employed by the prime contractor.

rows.verbatim: The CQC System Manager shall not have any duties other than quality control.
rows.normalized: CQC System Manager must not have duties other than quality control.

rows.verbatim:
When
the alternate for the CQC System Manager is activated, he/she shall also
have no duties other than quality control.
rows.normalized: If the Alternate CQC System Manager is activated, they must also have no duties other than quality control.

rows.verbatim:
QC Daily Reports
must be finalized and signed in RMS within 24 hours after the date covered
by the report.
rows.normalized: QC Daily Reports must be finalized and signed in RMS within 24 hours of the report date.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide the Government a printed signed copy of the QC Daily Report, unless waived by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a printed signed copy of the QC Daily Report unless waived by the CO.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall use the QC Daily Report Module to enter and track
deficiencies.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use the QC Daily Report Module to enter and track deficiencies.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall enter each deficiency
into RMS the same day that the deficiency is identified and shall monitor,
track, and resolve all QC and QA entered deficiencies.
rows.normalized: Contractor must enter each deficiency into RMS the same day identified, and must monitor, track, and resolve all QC/QA deficiencies.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall maintain scheduled and actual dates and times of
preparatory and initial control meetings in RMS.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain scheduled and actual dates/times of three-phase control meetings in RMS.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall enter labor and equipment exposure hours on a daily
basis and shall roll up the labor and equipment exposure data into a
monthly exposure report.
rows.normalized: Contractor must enter labor/equipment exposure hours daily and roll up into a monthly exposure report.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall monitor, track, and show resolution for safety issues in the QC Daily Report area of the RMS QC Module.
rows.normalized: Contractor must monitor, track, and show resolution of safety issues in the RMS QC Module.

rows.verbatim:
In
addition, the Contractor shall follow all reporting requirements for
accidents and incidents as required in the EM 385-1-1, Section 01 35 26 -
Governmental Safety Requirements, and as required by any other applicable
Federal, State, or local agencies.
rows.normalized: Contractor must follow all accident/incident reporting requirements per EM 385-1-1, Section 01 35 26, and applicable agencies.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall enter each feature of work into the RMS QC Module.
rows.normalized: Contractor must enter each feature of work into the RMS QC Module.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall import activity hazard analysis electronic document
files into the RMS QC Module utilizing the document package manager.
rows.normalized: Contractor must import activity hazard analysis files into the RMS QC Module.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall enter all current submittal register data and
information into RMS within 7 calendar days of receiving access to the
contract in RMS.
rows.normalized: Contractor must enter submittal register data into RMS within 7 calendar days of receiving access.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall group
electronic submittal documents into transmittal packages to send to the
Government, except very large electronic files, samples, spare parts, mock
ups, color boards, or where hard copies are specifically required.
rows.normalized: Contractor must group electronic submittals into transmittal packages, except large files, samples, spare parts, mock ups, color boards, or where hard copies are required.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall track transmittals and update the submittal register in
RMS on a daily basis throughout the duration of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must track transmittals and update the submittal register daily.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall submit hard copies of all submittals unless waived by
the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit hard copies of all submittals unless waived by the CO.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall enter and update the contract project schedule in RMS
by either manually entering all schedule data or by importing the Standard
Data Exchange Format (SDEF) file.
rows.normalized: Contractor must enter and update the project schedule in RMS manually or via SDEF import.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure that
all closeout documents are entered, completed, and documented within RMS.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure closeout documents are entered, completed, and documented in RMS.

rows.verbatim:
The
Contractor shall ensure that sufficient resources are available to
maintain contract data within the RMS system.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure sufficient resources are available to maintain RMS data.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall take corrective action within 7 calendar days after
receipt of notice of RMS non-compliance by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must take corrective action within 7 calendar days of receiving an RMS non-compliance notice.

rows.verbatim:
In order to prevent, and to provide for abatement and control of any
environmental pollution arising from construction activities in the
performance of this contract, the Contractor and his/her subcontractors
shall comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local laws, and
regulations concerning environmental pollution control and abatement.
rows.normalized: Contractor and subcontractors must comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local environmental pollution control laws.

rows.verbatim: All costs for the work covered under this section shall be distributed throughout the existing bid items.
rows.normalized: Costs for environmental protection work must be distributed throughout existing bid items.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall establish and maintain a plan for environmental
protection, to assure compliance with contract specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish and maintain an environmental protection plan.

rows.verbatim:
Within 120 hours after receiving notice to proceed, the Contractor
shall submit, in writing, proposals for environmental pollution
control, disposal of debris and trash, and an Environmental Protection
Plan, and
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit, in writing, proposals for pollution control, debris/trash disposal, and an Environmental Protection Plan within 120 hours of NTP.

rows.verbatim:
When directed by the Contracting Officer to a Secondary Dredging
Region, the Contractor shall re-submit the endangered species portion
of the Environmental Protection Plan applicable to that region.
rows.normalized: If directed to a Secondary Dredging Region, Contractor must re-submit the endangered species portion of the Environmental Protection Plan for that region.

rows.verbatim:
No part of time lost due to such a stop order
shall be made the subject of a claim for time extensions or for excess
costs or damages by the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not claim time extensions or excess costs/damages for time lost due to a stop order.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring that all subcontractors
comply with these environmental clauses.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure all subcontractors comply with the environmental clauses.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall inform the Government Inspector,
Contracting Officer's Representative, and Administrative Contracting
Officer, who will in turn contact CEMVN Historic Preservation (HP) staff.
rows.normalized: Contractor must inform the Government Inspector, COR, and ACO of the discovery.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall not proceed with work in the vicinity until CEMVN HP
staff completes consultation with the State Historic Preservation Offices
and others unless notified otherwise.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not proceed with work in the vicinity until CEMVN HP staff completes consultation, unless notified otherwise.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall not pollute any body of water with fuels; oils;
bitumens; calcium chlorides; herbicides; insecticides; other materials
harmful to fish, shellfish, or wildlife; or with materials that may be a
detriment to outdoor recreation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not pollute any body of water with fuels, oils, bitumens, calcium chlorides, herbicides, insecticides, or other harmful materials.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall assist the Government, using available on-site plant
and manpower, in monitoring the water quality aspects of the dredging and
disposal operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must assist the Government in monitoring water quality using on-site plant and manpower.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall keep construction activities under surveillance,
management, and control to minimize interference with, disturbance to, and
damage of fish and wildlife.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep construction activities under surveillance/management/control to minimize impact on fish and wildlife.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall not alter
natural water flows or otherwise disturb natural habitat adjacent to or
within the project area that are critical to fish or wildlife.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not alter natural water flows or disturb critical natural habitat.

rows.verbatim:
The
Contractor shall instruct all personnel associated with the project of the
potential presence of manatees in the area, and the need to avoid
collisions with these animals.
rows.normalized: Contractor must instruct all project personnel about potential manatee presence and the need to avoid collisions.

rows.verbatim:
All construction personnel shall be
advised that there are civil and criminal penalties for harming,
harassing, or killing manatees.
rows.normalized: Contractor must advise all construction personnel of civil/criminal penalties for harming manatees.

rows.verbatim:
The
Contractor shall be held responsible for any manatee harmed, harassed, or
killed as a result of construction activities not conducted in accordance
with these specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor is held responsible for any manatee harmed/harassed/killed due to non-compliant construction activities.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to commencement of construction, each vessel
involved in construction activities shall display at the vessel control
station or in a prominent location, visible to all employees operating the
vessel, a temporary sign at least 8-1/2 inches by 11 inches reading,
"CAUTION: MANATEE HABITAT/IDLE SPEED IS REQUIRED IN CONSTRUCTION AREA."
rows.normalized: Prior to construction commencement, each vessel must display a specified manatee caution sign at the vessel control station or a prominent visible location.

rows.verbatim:
In the absence of a vessel, a temporary three foot by four foot sign
reading "CAUTION: MANATEE AREA" shall be posted adjacent to the issued
construction permit.
rows.normalized: If no vessel is present, a 3x4 foot manatee caution sign must be posted adjacent to the construction permit.

rows.verbatim:
A second temporary sign measuring 8-1/2 inches by 11 inches reading "CAUTION: MANATEE HABITAT. EQUIPMENT MUST BE SHUTDOWN IMMEDIATELY IF A MANATEE COMES WITHIN 50 FEET OF OPERATION" shall be
posted at the dredge operator control station and at a location
SECTION 01 57 20.00 10 Page 4 prominently adjacent to the issued construction permit.
rows.normalized: Contractor must post a second 8-1/2 x 11 inch manatee-shutdown-warning sign at the dredge operator control station and prominently adjacent to the issued construction permit.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor
shall remove the signs upon completion of construction.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove the manatee signs upon completion of construction.

rows.verbatim:
(1) If a manatee(s) is sighted within 100 yards of the project
area, all appropriate precautions shall be implemented by the
Contractor to ensure protection of the manatee.
rows.normalized: If a manatee is sighted within 100 yards, Contractor must implement all appropriate precautions.

rows.verbatim: These precautions shall include the operation of all moving equipment no closer than 50 feet of a manatee.
rows.normalized: Precautions must include operating all moving equipment no closer than 50 feet from a manatee.

rows.verbatim: If a manatee is closer than 50 feet to moving equipment or the project area, the equipment shall be shut down and all construction activities shall cease to ensure protection of the manatee.
rows.normalized: If a manatee is closer than 50 feet to equipment or the project area, Contractor must shut down the equipment and cease all construction activities to protect the manatee.

rows.verbatim: Construction activities shall not resume until the manatee has departed and the 50-foot buffer has been reestablished.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not resume construction activities until the manatee has departed and the 50-foot buffer is reestablished.

rows.verbatim:
(2) If a manatee(s) is sighted in the project area, all vessels
associated with the project shall operate at "no wake/idle" speeds
at all times, and vessels will follow routes of deep water
whenever possible, until the manatee has departed the project
area.
rows.normalized: If a manatee is sighted in the project area, all project vessels must operate at no wake/idle speed and follow deep water routes until the manatee departs.

rows.verbatim: Boats used to transport personnel shall be shallow-draft vessels, preferably of the light-displacement category, where navigational safety permits.
rows.normalized: Boats used to transport personnel must be shallow-draft vessels, preferably light-displacement category, where navigational safety permits.

rows.verbatim:
(3) If siltation barriers are used, they
shall be made of material in which manatees cannot become
entangled, are properly secured, and are regularly monitored to
avoid manatee entrapment.
rows.normalized: If siltation barriers are used, they must be non-entangling material, properly secured, and regularly monitored.

rows.verbatim: Any sightings of manatees or collisions with a manatee shall be immediately reported to the Corps of Engineers.
rows.normalized: Contractor must immediately report any manatee sightings or collisions to the Corps of Engineers.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure that the following are done to reduce the likelihood of Sturgeon entrainment:
a. When lowering the ladder, the pumping rate should be reduced to the lowest speed feasible while the cutterhead is being lowered.
b. The cutterhead remains completely buried in the channel bottom during dredging operations.
c. If pumping water through the cutterhead is deemed necessary to dislodge material, or to clean the pumps, the pumping rate should be reduced to the lowest rate feasible while raising the ladder until the cutterhead is at least at mid-depth at which point the pumping rate can be increased.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure the following measures are done to reduce likelihood of Sturgeon entrainment: reduced pumping rate while lowering ladder, cutterhead kept buried during dredging, and reduced pumping rate while raising ladder until mid-depth; 3 items in total.

rows.verbatim:
a. The Contractor shall provide daily trash collection and cleanup of
the dredge and attendant plant.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide daily trash collection and cleanup of the dredge and attendant plant.

rows.verbatim:
b. Disposal locations for waste materials, effluents, trash, garbage,
oil, grease, chemicals, etc., shall be such that harmful debris will
SECTION 01 57 20.00 10 Page 5 not enter the waterway, adjacent wetlands, or the disposal areas;
prevent the use of the area for recreation; or present a hazard to
wildlife.
rows.normalized: Disposal locations must be such that harmful debris does not enter the waterway/wetlands, prevent recreational use, or endanger wildlife.

rows.verbatim:
Debris disposal shall be in accordance with applicable
Federal, State, and Local regulations, and
shall be performed in a
manner approved by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Debris disposal must comply with Federal/State/Local regulations and be performed in a manner approved by the CO.

rows.verbatim: During the life of this contract, the Contractor shall maintain all facilities constructed for pollution control for as long as the operations creating the particular pollutant are being carried out, or until the material concerned has become stabilized to the extent that pollution is no longer being created.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain pollution control facilities for the duration described.

rows.verbatim: Early in the contract period the Contractor shall conduct a training course that will emphasize all phases of environmental protection.
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct an environmental protection training course early in the contract period.

rows.verbatim: This course shall involve all Contractor personnel working on the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure the training course involves all Contractor personnel working on the contract.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer of the scheduled time for this course so that the Contracting Officer's Representative can attend.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify the Contracting Officer of the scheduled training course time.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall remove all debris caused by the use of polystyrene (styrofoam or similar material) floating pipelines, at the dredge site or any other locations used to install, store, or repair the floating pipeline.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove all debris caused by polystyrene floating pipeline use at dredge sites or related locations.

rows.verbatim: Suitable banding, mesh, or other covering shall be placed on the polystyrene floating pipeline to prevent deterioration during normal dredging operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must place suitable banding, mesh, or covering on polystyrene floating pipeline to prevent deterioration.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall furnish daily janitorial services for the dredge and attendant plant during the entire life of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish daily janitorial services for the dredge and attendant plant for the life of the contract.

rows.verbatim: The bathroom facilities shall be kept clean and sanitary at all times.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep bathroom facilities clean and sanitary at all times.

rows.verbatim: Facilities for the storage, preparation, and serving of food will likewise be kept clean and sanitary.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep food storage, preparation, and serving facilities clean and sanitary.

rows.verbatim: Services shall be performed at such a time and in such a manner to least interfere with operations, and need only be accomplished when the facilities are in daily use.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform janitorial services at times/manner that least interfere with operations, only when facilities are in daily use.

rows.verbatim: If an oil spill or chemical release occurs during the performance of this contract, the Contractor shall contact the National Response Center at 1-800-424-8802, as soon as possible.
rows.normalized: If an oil spill or chemical release occurs, Contractor must contact the National Response Center as soon as possible.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall comply with the instructions from the responding agency concerning containment and cleanup of the spill, and
shall provide the Contracting Officer with a complete written report of the incident.
rows.normalized: Contractor must comply with responding agency's containment/cleanup instructions and must provide the Contracting Officer a complete written report of the incident.

rows.verbatim:
The discharge pipeline shall conform to
lighting requirements set forth by the US Coast Guard in the "Rules of the
Road, International-Inland" https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/pdf/navrules/navrules.
pdf.
rows.normalized: Discharge pipeline must conform to US Coast Guard lighting requirements per Rules of the Road.

rows.verbatim: Unless otherwise specified, surveys and surveying shall be in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003, Engineering and Design, Hydrographic Surveying, latest edition.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform surveys and surveying in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003, latest edition, unless otherwise specified.

rows.verbatim: All costs for the work covered under this section shall be included in the contract unit price per hour in the applicable "Dredging" and "Option Dredging" items on the bidding schedule.
rows.normalized: Contractor must include all costs for surveying work in the unit price under the Dredging and Option Dredging bid items.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall establish and maintain quality control for the work specified in this section to assure compliance with the contract requirements and maintain records of his quality control for all surveying including but not limited to the following: a. Layouts and Surveys. Daily log of layout work and surveys consisting of type and location using the Government established baselines and gages as stated in the Contract Clause entitled "Layout of Work" (FAR 52.236-17). b. Reporting. The original and two copies of these reports and tests as well as the records of corrective action taken, shall be furnished daily to the Government. The report shall include a record of times and dates surveys were run, the horizontal control stations used and their coordinates, the vertical control points used and their elevations, and weather conditions.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish and maintain quality control and records including (a) daily logs of layout work/surveys per the Layout of Work clause and (b) daily reports (original plus two copies) covering times/dates of surveys, control stations/coordinates, control points/elevations, and weather; 2 required contents in total.

rows.verbatim: All surveys shall be performed in the presence of the Government Representative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform all surveys in the presence of the Government Representative.

rows.verbatim: All surveys shall be performed under the direction of and certified by a Professional Land Surveyor currently licensed by any state in the United States of America.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have all surveys performed under the direction of and certified by a licensed Professional Land Surveyor.

rows.verbatim: In addition, the surveyor shall document at least three years of experience in hydrographic surveying of navigable channels.
rows.normalized: The surveyor must document at least three years of experience in hydrographic surveying of navigable channels.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall submit, to the Contracting Officer for review, a plan
for the verification of surveying equipment described herein.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit a survey-equipment verification plan to the Contracting Officer for review.

rows.verbatim:
The plan
shall include types, certifications, calibration checks, etc., for the
surveying equipment.
rows.normalized: The verification plan must include types, certifications, and calibration checks for the surveying equipment.

rows.verbatim:
a. The Contractor shall furnish survey vessel(s), diesel or gasoline
powered, twin engine, not less than 30 feet in length, and equipped
with the following:
- Enclosed cabin;
- Space for four (4) passengers;
- Heating/air conditioning;
- Fully operated;
- U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) certified;
- Navigation radar, as described in Section 35 20 23.23, paragraph
entitled "Navigation Radar";
- Operable radio (same frequency as the dredge) for each dredge in
operation;
- A surveying lead line as described in EM 1110-2-1003, Appendix B-2.
- Hydrographic Surveying System: Hydrographic surveying software
(HYPACK or equivalent) and electronic horizontal positioning
(Differentially corrected Global Positioning, DGPS), depth sounding
and data acquisition instrumentation. The use of motion compensation
(a heave/pitch/roll sensor) is optional; however, if it is not used,
then the conduct of the survey will be restricted by roll/pitch/heave
sea-state limits [>10 degrees (roll-pitch), >.5 foot (heave)] as
interpreted by the on-site Government Representative. Additionally,
if the survey system utilizes motion compensation, then a side, bow or
stern mounting of the fathometer transducer is acceptable; however, if
motion compensation is not available, then the transducer must be hull
mounted.
- The vessel(s) must, at minimum, have a fathometer bar check
apparatus as described in EM 1110-2-1003, paragraph 4-10.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish survey vessel(s) meeting at-minimum specifications, equipped with listed items including cabin, capacity, radar, radio, lead line, and hydrographic system, with hull-mounted transducer required if motion compensation is unavailable, and a fathometer bar check apparatus required at minimum; 9 required items in total.

rows.verbatim:
The height of the fathometer transducer face while the vessel(s)
is static (draft) and in motion (settlement, squat) must be determined
as described in EM 1110-2-1003, paragraph 4-13.
rows.normalized: Contractor must determine the fathometer transducer face height in static and dynamic vessel conditions per EM 1110-2-1003 para 4-13.

rows.verbatim:
A method must be established to determine and correct for any vessel draft changes
during the surveying period [ex: Real-Time Kinematic (RTK)
observations at static draft to increasing engine RPM (paragraph
4-13c)].
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish a method to determine and correct for vessel draft changes during the surveying period.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to surveying operations, a hydrographic system latency bias
calibration test must be performed and the latency correctors must be
applied (EM 1110-2-1003, paragraph 4-15).
rows.normalized: Prior to surveying operations, Contractor must perform a hydrographic system latency bias calibration test and apply the latency correctors.

rows.verbatim:
"No Smoking" signs shall be posted and no smoking will be allowed
when occupied by Government personnel.
rows.normalized: Contractor must post 'No Smoking' signs and prohibit smoking on the vessel when occupied by Government personnel.

rows.verbatim:
All survey soundings shall be taken with a precision, high-resolution (0.1
SECTION 35 01 50.73 Page 3 feet) fathometer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must take all survey soundings with a precision, high-resolution (0.1 feet) fathometer.

rows.verbatim:
The acoustic ping rate shall be, at minimum, 10
soundings per second.
rows.normalized: The fathometer's acoustic ping rate must be at least 10 soundings per second.

rows.verbatim:
To limit signal attenuation in areas of
unconsolidated bottom sediments, the acoustic frequency utilized shall be
within the range of 24-28 KHz and the Low Frequency Low Pulse Width shall
be in accordance with the Manufacturers recommended settings for
unconsolidated bottom sediments in shallow water depths (i.e., 0 to 150
feet).
rows.normalized: Contractor must use an acoustic frequency of 24-28 KHz and Low Frequency Low Pulse Width per manufacturer settings for unconsolidated bottom sediments in shallow water (0-150 feet).

rows.verbatim: the Low Frequency Low Pulse Width shall be in accordance with the Manufacturers recommended settings for unconsolidated bottom sediments in shallow water depths (i.e., 0 to 150 feet).
rows.normalized: The Low Frequency Low Pulse Width must follow manufacturer-recommended settings for unconsolidated bottom sediments in shallow water depths (0-150 feet).

rows.verbatim:
If a dual frequency fathometer is utilized, then the low frequency
shall be within the 24-28 KHz range.
rows.normalized: If a dual frequency fathometer is used, its low frequency must be within the 24-28 KHz range.

rows.verbatim:
At minimum, the equipment shall be
capable of recording depths of water ranging from three feet under the
transducer face(s) to a maximum of 50 feet.
rows.normalized: The equipment must be capable of recording depths from 3 feet under the transducer face to a maximum of 50 feet, at minimum.

rows.verbatim:
At this maximum depth, the
sounding accuracy must be 0.5 feet (28 KHz transducer).
rows.normalized: At the maximum recording depth, sounding accuracy must be 0.5 feet (28 KHz transducer).

rows.verbatim:
Acoustic returns shall be recorded on thermal chart paper by a fixed, high-resolution
printing element (no stylus).
rows.normalized: Contractor must record acoustic returns on thermal chart paper using a fixed, high-resolution printing element (no stylus).

rows.verbatim:
A digital fathometer may be used instead of
paper charts as directed by the Contracting Officer's Representative, but
the Contractor must still be capable of producing paper charts unless
otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: A digital fathometer may be used instead of paper charts if directed by the COR, but the Contractor must still be capable of producing paper charts unless otherwise directed by the COR.

rows.verbatim:
The paper
chart scaling shall be in English units, no greater than 0-50 feet
full-scale and graduated in 1 foot increments with numeric depth
annotations at the 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 foot chart levels.
rows.normalized: Paper chart scaling must be in English units, no greater than 0-50 feet full-scale, graduated in 1-foot increments with numeric depth annotations at 0,10,20,30,40,50 foot chart levels.

rows.verbatim:
The
instrument shall, at minimum, be capable of adjusting transmit power,
receiver sensitivity and time-varied gain settings and of inputting the
correct speed-of-sound, vessel draft and tide values.
rows.normalized: The fathometer instrument must be capable, at minimum, of adjusting transmit power, receiver sensitivity, and time-varied gain settings, and of inputting speed-of-sound, vessel draft, and tide values.

rows.verbatim:
Additionally, the
surveyor shall print the control parameter settings on the chart paper at
the start of all surveys and when any control settings are changed and
before and after all bar checks.
rows.normalized: The surveyor must print control parameter settings on the chart paper at the start of each survey, when settings change, and before/after all bar checks.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to the Contractor taking
preliminary field surveys, control parameter settings shall be turned into
the Government Inspector for review to ensure the settings meet the
surveying parameters.
rows.normalized: Prior to preliminary field surveys, the Contractor must submit control parameter settings to the Government Inspector for review.

rows.verbatim:
During the surveying of run lines, the fathometer
shall be capable of annotating periodic event marks on the paper chart as
directed by other surveying system components (positioning, controlling
software) and be capable of transmitting each event sounding back to these
system components for horizontal position tagging and data storage.
rows.normalized: During run-line surveying, the fathometer must be capable of annotating periodic event marks on the paper chart and transmitting each event sounding back to the positioning/controlling software for position tagging and data storage.

rows.verbatim: Hydrographic fathometer calibrations shall be performed at the survey site by methods described in EM 1110-2-1003, paragraphs 4-10 through 4-15 and at a frequency listed in table 4-6 for navigation and dredging support surveys with soft bottom materials.
rows.normalized: Fathometer calibrations must be performed at the survey site per EM 1110-2-1003 (paragraphs 4-10 to 4-15) and at the frequency in table 4-6.

rows.verbatim: The acoustic traces of the bar or ball check calibrations shall be captured on the fathometer paper chart (at the 10, 20, and 30 foot depths, or as directed by the Government Representative) along with a notation indicating the site location (i.e., station, lat/long, x, y), the date and time.
rows.normalized: Acoustic traces of bar/ball check calibrations must be captured on the paper chart at specified depths with location, date, and time notations.

rows.verbatim: Additionally, if a velocity meter probe is utilized, the average speed-of-sound reading for the entire water column and the location, date and time of the probe sounding must also be noted on the fathometer paper chart.
rows.normalized: If a velocity meter probe is used, its average speed-of-sound reading and location/date/time must be noted on the fathometer paper chart.

rows.verbatim: All calibration and soundings shall be made in the presence and to the satisfaction of the Government Representative at the job site.
rows.normalized: All calibrations and soundings must be made in the presence and to the satisfaction of the Government Representative at the job site.

rows.verbatim: The Low Frequency Pulse Width range of cycles (i.e., 1 to 10) used shall not produce signal lengths less than 35 microseconds or greater than 125 microseconds.
rows.normalized: The Low Frequency Pulse Width cycle range used must not produce signal lengths less than 35 or greater than 125 microseconds.

rows.verbatim: The hydrographic surveying vessel(s) must meet or exceed horizontal accuracy of U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Maritime Differential Global Positioning System (DGPS) instrumentation for determining horizontal positioning during surveying operations in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003, paragraph 7-3.
rows.normalized: Contractor's survey vessel(s) must meet or exceed USCG DGPS horizontal accuracy per EM 1110-2-1003 7-3.

rows.verbatim: This DGPS instrumentation must have a positioning accuracy of 1-3 meters 2DRMS.
rows.normalized: DGPS instrumentation must have positioning accuracy of 1-3 meters 2DRMS.

rows.verbatim: If the USCG system is to be utilized, then the English Turn beacon site shall be the source for differential corrections.
rows.normalized: If the Contractor uses the USCG system, the English Turn beacon site shall be the source for differential corrections.

rows.verbatim: The GPS antenna on the survey vessel(s) must be physically positioned directly above the fathometer transducer or the hydrographic surveying software suite must be capable of aligning the horizontal and vertical sensors.
rows.normalized: GPS antenna must be positioned above the fathometer transducer, or the survey software must align horizontal and vertical sensors.

rows.verbatim: The hydrographic surveying vessel(s) must reduce final survey elevations relative to project datum using tide staffs referenced in the Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: Survey vessel(s) must reduce final survey elevations to project datum using referenced tide staffs.

rows.verbatim: As directed by the Contracting Officer's Representative, visual water level observations, Real-Time Kinematic (RTK), Real-Time Networks (RTN), or post-processed kinematic elevation computations shall be used in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003, paragraphs 7-11 through 7-14.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use visual water level, RTK, RTN, or post-processed kinematic elevation methods as directed, per EM 1110-2-1003 7-11 to 7-14.

rows.verbatim: Real-time or post-processed methods must include a static observation adjacent to the tide staff(s) for calibration of orthometric heights to project datum.
rows.normalized: Real-time or post-processed methods must include a static observation near tide staff(s) for calibration.

rows.verbatim: Surveys for all fixed stations shall be performed in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003, Chapter 4 - Section IV "Data Collection, Editing, and Processing".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall perform surveys for all fixed stations per EM 1110-2-1003 Chapter 4 Section IV.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall be able to use this data to lay out the work and subsequently provide completed work as specified herein to the Government.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall be able to use the survey data to lay out and complete work as specified.

rows.verbatim: Prior to initiating positioning surveys using electronic survey equipment, a calibration test of the electronic measuring device shall be performed according to the manufacturer's instructions in the presence of the Contracting Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: Before initiating positioning surveys, Contractor shall perform a calibration test per manufacturer instructions in the presence of the COR.

rows.verbatim: Calibration checks shall be run at the beginning and completion of each day's survey or portion thereof.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall run calibration checks at start and end of each day's survey.

rows.verbatim: Results shall be furnished daily to the Contracting Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish calibration results daily to the COR.

rows.verbatim: All electronic surveys shall be tied to a fixed station.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall tie all electronic surveys to a fixed station.

rows.verbatim: Should the electronic measuring device fail to indicate the known distance within the factory defined error range for the device, the device shall not be used for determining survey positions.
rows.normalized: If the measuring device fails the known-distance check within factory error range, it shall not be used for survey positions.

rows.verbatim: Surveys will include but will not be limited to the following surveys.
rows.normalized: The Contractor's surveys will include, but are not limited to, the survey types identified in the following subsections.

rows.verbatim: Prior to taking any original cross sections, the Contractor shall run a preliminary field survey electronically controlled locating the baseline/centerline, towers, all buoys, channel markers, utility crossings, P.C.'s, P.T.'s, P.I.'s, and P.O.T.'s within the limits of the survey area.
rows.normalized: Before original cross sections, Contractor shall run a preliminary field survey locating specified features within the survey area.

rows.verbatim: The data from this survey shall be plotted on a plan sheet and submitted to the Contracting Officer for confirmation of correct channel alignment.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall plot preliminary survey data on a plan sheet and submit to the CO for alignment confirmation.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall also submit a Hypack Channel file (.chn) that depicts the channel alignment of the entire dredging region prior to the pre-construction conference.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit a Hypack Channel file (.chn) depicting channel alignment before the pre-construction conference.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall not proceed with any dredging work until the Contracting Officer determines the final channel alignment and furnishes this information to the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall not proceed with dredging until the CO determines and furnishes final channel alignment.

rows.verbatim: Depth soundings shall be made with the hydrographic surveying system (as described in the paragraph entitled "Survey Equipment") and the recorded sounding resolution shall be one sounding for every 5 feet along the cross section runlines (normal to the centerline).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall take depth soundings with the hydrographic system at one sounding per 5 feet along cross section runlines.

rows.verbatim: The recorded depths shall be to a resolution of 0.1 feet.
rows.normalized: Recorded depths shall be to a resolution of 0.1 feet.

rows.verbatim: The sensitivity/gain control setting that is selected for the survey area bottom material-type must also be used for the bar check calibrations and must not be adjusted during hydrographic surveying (EM 1110-2-1003, paragraph 4-6).
rows.normalized: The sensitivity/gain setting selected for bottom material type must also be used for bar check calibrations and must not be adjusted during surveying.

rows.verbatim: In areas of consolidated bottom material, the digitized and recorded depth soundings shall indicate the true channel bottom.
rows.normalized: In consolidated bottom material areas, recorded soundings shall indicate the true channel bottom.

rows.verbatim: However, in survey areas containing unconsolidated bottom materials, acoustic measurements must be calibrated with lead line measurements.
rows.normalized: In unconsolidated bottom material areas, acoustic measurements must be calibrated with lead line measurements.

rows.verbatim: These leadline measurements must be notated on the fathometer paper chart and taken at a minimum of 5,000 foot intervals; on the channel centerline and both edges of cut, or as determined by the Government Representative on the jobsite.
rows.normalized: Leadline measurements must be notated on the fathometer chart and taken at a minimum of 5,000 foot intervals on centerline and edges of cut.

rows.verbatim: The real-time fathometer paper charting of the surveying runs, to include calibration and leadline events and all survey notations, shall be furnished to the Government.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish real-time fathometer paper charting, including calibration/leadline events and notations, to the Government.

rows.verbatim: Stored hydrographic data (x,y,z) shall also be furnished to the Government in a structured ASCII format on compact disk (CD) media.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish stored hydrographic (x,y,z) data to the Government in structured ASCII format on CD media.

rows.verbatim: A chart layout of the before dredging cross sections shall be prepared by the Contractor and approved by the Contracting Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall prepare a chart layout of before-dredging cross sections for COR approval.

rows.verbatim: This graphical chart must represent a scaled plan view of the survey area with the recorded 5 foot interval depth soundings (0.1 foot resolution) plotted at their x,y positions.
rows.normalized: The chart must be a scaled plan view showing 5-foot interval depth soundings (0.1 ft resolution) at x,y positions.

rows.verbatim: The actual location of each sounding taken on each before dredging cross section range shall be provided.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide the actual location of each sounding on each before-dredging cross section range.

rows.verbatim:
Soundings shall be to the nearest 0.1-foot referred to the
water surface.
rows.normalized: Soundings shall be recorded to the nearest 0.1 foot referred to the water surface.

rows.verbatim:
This information shall also be plotted on a printout
sheet, horizontal vertical scale, along with a section showing the
required dredging dimensions.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall plot the information on a printout sheet with horizontal/vertical scale showing required dredging dimensions.

rows.verbatim:
The time and date taken shall be shown
and the gage reading applicable to the survey shall be shown.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall show the time, date, and applicable gage reading for the survey.

rows.verbatim:
The applicable gage shall be read to the nearest 0.1-foot prior to and
after each day's survey.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall read the applicable gage to the nearest 0.1 foot before and after each day's survey.

rows.verbatim:
d. The Contractor shall remove, at no additional cost to the
Government, any material in the navigation channel outside the area
designated to be dredged if the material falls within the channel and
was not indicated on the before dredging survey (roll effect
downstream of the cutterhead dredge).
rows.normalized: If undredged material falls into the channel and was not shown on the before-dredging survey, Contractor shall remove it at no additional cost.

rows.verbatim:
The data obtained from the electronic positioning/control system and the
fathometer shall be collected, recorded, and processed.
rows.normalized: Data from the positioning/control system and fathometer shall be collected, recorded, and processed.

rows.verbatim:
Soundings shall be recorded to the nearest 0.1-foot and the X and Y coordinates of these
soundings shall be recorded to the nearest foot.
rows.normalized: Soundings shall be recorded to nearest 0.1 foot; X/Y coordinates to nearest foot.

rows.verbatim:
More frequent readings will be
required when directed by the Government Inspector.
rows.normalized: When directed by the Government Inspector, Contractor will be required to take more frequent readings.

rows.verbatim:
From the processed data, the Contractor shall
provide certain survey information taken for the purpose of computing the
total amount of work to be paid for.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide certain survey information from processed data for computing total work quantity for payment.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor must furnish the
required data on CD/DVD/e-mail containing ASCII character set.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish required data on CD/DVD/e-mail in ASCII character set.

rows.verbatim:
The information received shall be free of errors and in the following format:
(a) the X-coordinate in feet of a recognized Louisiana Lambert grid
system, (b) the Y-coordinate in feet of same recognized Louisiana grid
system, (c) the elevation, and (d) remarks such as the station number
(i.e. 1+00), CL (for centerline), ES (for end of station), EJ (end of
file), and direction of survey (either "L" for + or "R" for -, followed by
Station No., i.e. L 30+00).
rows.normalized: Data must be free of errors and provided in the format: (a) X-coordinate, (b) Y-coordinate, (c) elevation, (d) remarks (station, CL, ES, EJ, direction) - 4 format elements total.

rows.verbatim:
The time and date the cross section was taken
and the gage reading applicable to the section must be included.
rows.normalized: Time, date of cross section, and applicable gage reading must be included.

rows.verbatim:
The
electronically recorded data files, along with a hard copy of the track
plotter surveys, plotted on the chart to show compliance with alignment,
and quantity computations shall be presented to the Government
Representative on site no later than three days after the survey is
taken.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall present data files, track plotter hard copy, and quantity computations to the Government Representative on site no later than 3 days after the survey.

rows.verbatim:
Not submitting the data in accordance to the specifications and
within the allotted time will be cause to withhold progress payment.
rows.normalized: Failure to submit data per specifications and on time will cause withholding of progress payment.

rows.verbatim:
Under no circumstances shall the information be edited for the purpose of
eliminating incorrect soundings.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall never edit data to eliminate incorrect soundings.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide a separate file listing all incorrect
soundings to be eliminated.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide a separate file listing all incorrect soundings to be eliminated.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall
submit a separate survey file for each 2,000 feet acceptance reach (or
portion less than 2,000 feet for the final reach of an assignment)
unless otherwise directed by the Government Inspector.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit a separate survey file for each 2,000-foot acceptance reach unless otherwise directed.

rows.verbatim:
The beginning
station for each file shall be the repeated ending station from the
previous file (i.e., Sta. 820+00 to 840+00, Sta. 840+00 to 860+00, etc.).
rows.normalized: Beginning station for each file shall be the repeated ending station from the previous file.

rows.verbatim:
Upon completion of dredging in a designated reach, waterway profiles shall
be taken over the same dredging reach.
rows.normalized: Upon completion of dredging in a reach, Contractor shall take waterway profiles over that reach.

rows.verbatim:
Distances between soundings on
each profile shall be 20 feet.
rows.normalized: Distances between soundings on each profile shall be 20 feet.

rows.verbatim:
Controlled profiles of the waterway shall be made along the dredge cut
centerline and one at each outside bottom edge of the cut.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall make controlled profiles along the dredge cut centerline and both outside bottom edges of cut.

rows.verbatim:
This information shall be plotted
on a printout sheet, 1 inch = 300 feet horizontal: 1 inch = 10 feet
vertical scale.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall plot the profile information at 1 inch=300 ft horizontal, 1 inch=10 ft vertical scale.

rows.verbatim:
Waterway profiles shall be performed for secondary
dredging regions as directed by the Contracting Officer if these regions
are utilized.
rows.normalized: If secondary dredging regions are utilized, Contractor shall perform waterway profiles as directed by the CO.

rows.verbatim:
For the purpose of computing the average actual production rate, the
actual quantity of dredged material removed shall be measured by the
cubic yard by computing the volume along the centerline between the
before and after dredging cross sections using the average end area
method and limited by the allowable dredging tolerances described in
Section 35 20 23.23, paragraph entitled "Required Production and Dredging
Tolerances".
rows.normalized: Actual dredged quantity shall be measured in cubic yards via average end area method between before/after cross sections, per tolerances in Section 35 20 23.23.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall make dredging volume computations which
shall be furnished to the Government with the before and after survey data
described in the paragraph entitled "Before and After Dredging Cross
Sections".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall make and furnish dredging volume computations with before/after survey data.

rows.verbatim:
In computing end areas and volumes for the purpose of
computing the average actual production rate payment, the Contractor shall
translate all cross section survey shots to the correct azimuth normal to
the centerline of the cut and shall insert a shot at the actual station
C/L with an interpolated elevation.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall translate cross section survey shots to correct azimuth and insert a shot at station C/L with interpolated elevation.

rows.verbatim:
No before dredging cross sections
will be allowed to be taken and used for quantity computations within 500
feet in front of the dredge.
rows.normalized: Before-dredging cross sections may not be taken/used for quantity computations within 500 feet in front of the dredge.

rows.verbatim:
Each field book shall be given an identification number, which shall be
noted on each page of the book.
rows.normalized: Each field book shall be given an ID number, noted on each page.

rows.verbatim:
The information shown in the field notes
shall meet the requirements of the Contracting Government Representative.
rows.normalized: Field notes information shall meet the requirements of the Contracting Government Representative.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall promptly plot the channel cross sections on a scale
as described in the applicable Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall promptly plot channel cross sections on the specified scale.

rows.verbatim:
Plotted cross sections, profiles, and duplicate notes shall be kept at the
jobsite at all times and made available to the Government Representative
upon request.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall keep plotted cross sections, profiles, and duplicate notes at the jobsite at all times, available on request.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall furnish to the Contracting Officer's
Representative the plotted original cross sections for a minimum distance
of 500 feet ahead of the dredging location in the direction of work
progression.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish plotted original cross sections to the COR for a minimum 500 feet ahead of the dredging location.

rows.verbatim:
One copy of all plotted Before and After dredging cross sections
shall be kept in the lever room of the dredge at all times.
rows.normalized: One copy of all plotted before/after cross sections shall be kept in the dredge's lever room at all times.

rows.verbatim:
It is the purpose of these specifications to secure for the Government the
hire and operation of one cutterhead dredge, with a dredge discharge size
not less than 27 inches inside diameter (ID), complete in all respects,
including all attendant plant and crew.
rows.normalized: The cutterhead dredge discharge size must be not less than 27 inches inside diameter.

rows.verbatim:
The dredge shall be efficient and effective for all work described in these
specifications.
rows.normalized: The dredge shall be efficient and effective for all specified work.

rows.verbatim:
All floating plant shall comply with applicable US Coast Guard and US Public Health
Service regulations.
rows.normalized: All floating plant shall comply with applicable USCG and US Public Health Service regulations.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall furnish all plant, materials,
equipment, supplies, labor, and transportation, and perform all work in
strict accordance with these specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish all plant, materials, equipment, supplies, labor, transportation and perform all work per specifications.

rows.verbatim:
All work, materials, and
services not expressly called for in these specifications, but which may be
necessary for complete and proper operations to carry out the contract in
good faith shall be performed, furnished, or installed by the
Contractor at no increase in cost to the Government.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall perform/furnish/install any work not expressly specified but necessary for proper operations, at no additional cost.

rows.verbatim:
All work under these
specifications shall be performed in accordance with the provisions of EM
385-1-1 "Safety and Occupational Health Requirements", latest edition.
rows.normalized: All work shall be performed per EM 385-1-1 Safety and Occupational Health Requirements, latest edition.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall be
responsible for staking its own approach for initial and interim
mobilization and demobilization, for its dredge and all attendant plant,
from the plants location where last employed, to the dredging region(s),
as described in the applicable Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall be responsible for staking its own approach for mobilization/demobilization of dredge and plant to dredging regions.

rows.verbatim:
All costs for a fully operated cutterhead dredge shall be included in the
contract unit price per hour in the "NOH Dredging", "NOH Option Dredging",
"Houma Dredging", "Houma Option Dredging", "Bayou Lafourche Dredging",
"Bayou Lafourche Option Dredging", "Barataria Bar Dredging", "Barataria
Bar Option Dredging", "Baptiste Collette Dredging", and "Baptiste Collette
Option Dredging" items on the bidding schedule.
rows.normalized: All costs for a fully operated cutterhead dredge shall be included in the contract unit price per hour for the listed bidding schedule items.

rows.verbatim:
Price and payment shall constitute
full compensation for furnishing all necessary plant, labor, fuel,
supplies, safety equipment and procedures, crew, furnishing and
maintaining communication equipment, crew boat, survey boat and operator,
surveys, satisfactory disposal of dredged material, and all operational
incidentals thereto.
rows.normalized: Contract price and payment shall constitute full compensation for all listed plant, labor, and operational items.

rows.verbatim: Dredging shall be performed at or above the required minimum production rate as specified herein unless assignments involve non standard dredging, as described in the paragraph entitled "Dredging in Non-Standard Reaches and Conditions".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall dredge at or above the required minimum production rate, unless the assignment involves non-standard dredging.

rows.verbatim: To avoid excessive unnecessary dredging at each assignment, quantities shall be measured to the actual elevation of dredging, not to exceed one foot below the dredging assignment's specified elevation and the actual swing width, not to exceed ten feet beyond the specified swing width on each side.
rows.normalized: Dredging quantities shall be measured such that actual elevation does not exceed one foot below, and swing width does not exceed ten feet beyond, the specified limits.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall remove all material in the assigned template in one pass unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall remove all material in the assigned template in one pass unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall make such openings upon signal of any vessel or craft desiring to pass;
rows.normalized: Contractor shall open for passage upon signal of any vessel or craft desiring to pass.

rows.verbatim: All 70% pay time under this subparagraph shall be measured from the time material stops flowing out of the discharge pipeline, until the time material starts flowing out of the discharge pipeline at the new location.
rows.normalized: The 70% pay time under this subparagraph must be measured from when material stops flowing out of the discharge pipeline until it starts flowing out at the new location.

rows.verbatim: The pay time shall include preparations time and time to move the dredge to the new dredging location with the preparation time limited to six hours each to stop and start up.
rows.normalized: Pay time must include preparation and dredge-move time, with preparation time limited to six hours each for stop and start up.

rows.verbatim: Payment for the dredge moving time shall be the actual hours not to exceed the following: (the shortest distance, regardless of dredge size or configuration, from the current dredging location to the new dredging location) / (the minimum tow rate of 3 mph for moving upstream and 5 mph moving downstream);
rows.normalized: Payment for dredge moving time must be the actual hours, not to exceed the calculated distance-over-tow-rate limit.

rows.verbatim: The plant shall be placed on 70% pay time hours when material stops flowing out of the discharge pipeline in order to begin preparations to move the plant to the SECTION 35 20 23.23 Page 5 harbor of refuge site approved by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: The plant must be placed on 70% pay time hours when material stops flowing, to begin preparations to move to the Contracting Officer-approved harbor of refuge.

rows.verbatim: Towing costs for moving to and from harbor of refuge will be at the Contractor's expense.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for towing costs to and from a harbor of refuge (hurricane/tropical storm scenario).

rows.verbatim: In this case, the Contracting Officer will require the Contractor to re-mobilize the dredge and attendant plant to the deficient reach, re-dredge the deficient area, and demobilize from the deficient dredging area at no additional cost to the Government.
rows.normalized: If after-dredging cross sections are non-compliant due to Contractor fault, Contractor must re-mobilize, re-dredge, and demobilize from the deficient area at no additional cost to the Government.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor should note that the dredge must account for the full 24 hours of each day, including the first and last day of work.
rows.normalized: Contractor must account for the full 24 hours of each day, including the first and last day of work.

rows.verbatim: When conditions are such that the Contractor is placed on 0% pay time hours, the Contractor shall remain at 0% pay time hours until material begins flowing out of the discharge pipeline.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall remain at 0% pay time status until material begins flowing out of the discharge pipeline.

rows.verbatim: Hydrographic survey data must be in accordance with the requirements specified in Section 35 01 50.73, Surveys.
rows.normalized: Hydrographic survey data must comply with Section 35 01 50.73, Surveys.

rows.verbatim: These Contractor performed surveys, witnessed by the Government, shall be provided to the Contracting Officer within 24 hours after they are taken.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide Contractor-performed, Government-witnessed surveys to the Contracting Officer within 24 hours after they are taken.

rows.verbatim: When dredging in standard dredging conditions, the Contractor shall attain at least the minimum production rate specified.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall attain at least the minimum specified production rate when dredging in standard dredging conditions.

rows.verbatim: When the Government does not receive from the Contractor, the SECTION 35 20 23.23 Page 9 hydrographic survey data used to determine actual production within specified time requirements, 100% pay time hours shall be paid at the basic hourly rate specified in the bid schedule for the dredging payment items.
rows.normalized: If the Contractor fails to provide the hydrographic survey data used to determine actual production within the specified time requirements, 100% pay time hours will be paid at the basic hourly rate instead of the adjusted rate.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall furnish towing services described in the paragraph entitled "Dredge Attendant Plant" to move the dredge and equipment on approximately 12 hours advance notice.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish towing services to move the dredge and equipment on approximately 12 hours advance notice.

rows.verbatim: The dredge shall remain on 72 hour call by the Contracting Officer during the release period.
rows.normalized: Contractor's dredge shall remain on 72-hour call during any release period.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall prepare and submit a Daily Report of Operations (MVN Form 4267) and the Original Leverman's Log signed by each shift leverman, for each dredge working.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall prepare and submit a Daily Report of Operations and signed Leverman's Log for each working dredge.

rows.verbatim: The MVN Form 4267 provided at the end of this section shall be used in lieu of the RMS Form 4267 and uploaded to RMS separately.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use the provided MVN Form 4267 instead of RMS Form 4267 and upload it to RMS separately.

rows.verbatim: These documents shall be submitted electronically on a daily basis and not in groups, e.g. several daily reports packaged together at one time.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit daily report documents electronically each day, not batched together.

rows.verbatim: The original and one copy of these records in report form shall be submitted electronically to the Government Inspector daily within 12 hours after the date covered by the report.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit original and one copy of daily report records electronically to the Government Inspector within 12 hours after the report date.

rows.verbatim: Each daily report shall only include the information beginning at 0000 hours and ending at 2400 hours of that day.
rows.normalized: Contractor's daily reports shall cover only 0000 to 2400 hours of the reporting day.

rows.verbatim: All calendar days shall be accounted for throughout the life of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall account for all calendar days throughout the life of the contract.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall also prepare a report of operations for each month or partial month's work on MVN Form 322 (Work Sheet for Preparing Consolidated Form 4267).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall prepare a monthly report of operations on MVN Form 322 for each month or partial month worked.

rows.verbatim: The monthly report shall be submitted electronically on or before the 7th of each month, consolidating the previous month's work.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit the monthly report electronically no later than the 7th of each month.

rows.verbatim: Upon completion of the work, the Contractor shall electronically submit information for a final report, which consolidates all of the monthly reports, within seven calendar days of contract completion.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall electronically submit a final consolidated report within seven calendar days of contract completion.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall distribute one electronic copy of all reports (daily, monthly, and final) to the Administrative Contracting Officer, Contracting Officer's Representative, and Government Inspector.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall distribute one electronic copy of all reports to the ACO, COR, and Government Inspector.

rows.verbatim: Each Report of Operations shall be maintained by the Contractor on the dredge.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain each Report of Operations on the dredge.

rows.verbatim: Upon completion of the job, the Contractor shall also submit a consolidated job report, combining the monthly reports in accordance with the previously listed distribution.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit a consolidated job report combining monthly reports upon job completion, per the listed distribution.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall complete the plant data sheet located in the paragraph entitled "Cutterhead Dredge and Attendant Plant Data Sheet" for the dredge and attendant plant that the Contractor will use to perform the work under this contract.

rows.verbatim: The dredge plant length measured horizontally from the digging spud to the cutterhead's location while dredging at a channel depth of 67 feet, measured from the water surface, shall be no less than 262 feet to meet the swing requirements specified in subparagraph (c).
rows.normalized: The dredge plant length must be no less than 262 feet, measured as specified, to meet swing requirements.

rows.verbatim: Dredges shall meet or exceed the minimum production rate requirements listed in the table located in the Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: Dredges must meet or exceed the minimum production rate requirements listed in the Dredging Region Section tables.

rows.verbatim:
Submerged pumps shall meet the following conditions in order for the dredge to be classified as utilizing a submerged pump:
(1) The submerged pump shall be located on the cutterhead ladder
and shall be placed at a distance of no more than two-thirds the
length of the ladder from the cutterhead.
(2) The submerged pump shall be fully immersed.
(3) The submerged pump is operating.
rows.normalized: Submerged pumps must satisfy three listed conditions (location on ladder within two-thirds of its length from the cutterhead, full immersion, and operation) to be classified as submerged-pump dredges.

rows.verbatim: The cutterhead ladder shall be of sufficient length to provide a uniformly dredged channel depth of 67 feet, measured from the water surface.
rows.normalized: The cutterhead ladder must be long enough to provide a uniformly dredged channel depth of 67 feet.

rows.verbatim: The spuds shall be of sufficient length to perform dredging operations in water depths from 11 to 70 feet.
rows.normalized: The spuds must be long enough to perform dredging in water depths from 11 to 70 feet.

rows.verbatim: The dredge shall be capable, from each setting of the spud, of dredging a channel at least 300 foot wide, while swinging through an arc of 35 degrees to either side of the centerline of the cut (total arc 70 degrees or less) while at a depth of 67 feet, measured from the water surface.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be capable of dredging a channel at least 300 feet wide, swinging up to 35 degrees each side (70 degrees total) at a 67-foot depth, from each spud setting.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall fulfill the requirements of this subparagraph and subparagraph (a) while achieving or exceeding the minimum production rate requirements listed in the tables at the end of the applicable Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: The Contractor must fulfill the requirements of subparagraphs (a) and (c) while meeting or exceeding the minimum production rates in the Dredging Region Section tables.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall have available for use at all times a variety of interchangeable pump impellers to permit the dredge to operate under the varying conditions described in the applicable Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: The Contractor must keep a variety of interchangeable pump impellers available at all times for varying dredging conditions.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor at all times shall have available SECTION 35 20 23.23 Page 14 additional serviceable basket type 5- or 6- blade cutterhead, serviceable sand-type cutterhead, and serviceable cone-type cutterhead to efficiently and effectively dredge.
rows.normalized: The Contractor must have available at all times serviceable basket-type (5- or 6-blade), sand-type, and cone-type cutterheads for efficient dredging.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall also have available replacement blades and knives for the dredge pump and wipers for the cutter.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall also have available replacement blades/knives for the dredge pump and wipers for the cutter.

rows.verbatim: The dredge shall be equipped with recording vacuum and pressure gauges and a print out of the electronic data recording of engine and pump functions and a pump engine recording tachometer.
rows.normalized: Dredge shall be equipped with recording vacuum/pressure gauges, engine/pump data recording printout, and a pump engine recording tachometer.

rows.verbatim: During dredging, these instruments shall record data on control chart paper consisting of pipeline pressure and pump vacuum (lbs/cu in.), and pump RPM at rated drive of the prime mover.
rows.normalized: During dredging, instruments shall record pipeline pressure, pump vacuum, and pump RPM data on control chart paper.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall deliver completed recordings to the Inspector on watch at the time of removal from the recording devices, each day of operation.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall deliver completed recordings to the Inspector on watch at time of removal, each day of operation.

rows.verbatim: On dredges equipped with and using a ladder pump, the vacuum gage and vacuum chart will not be required.
rows.normalized: Vacuum gage and vacuum chart are not required on dredges equipped with and using a ladder pump.

rows.verbatim: f. The dredge shall be equipped with a gyro compass.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be equipped with a gyro compass.

rows.verbatim: All gauges, meters, and other dredging sensory equipment, shall have a valid and current calibration certificate sticker.
rows.normalized: All dredging sensory equipment (gauges, meters, etc.) shall have a valid, current calibration certificate sticker.

rows.verbatim: Re-calibration where applicable and as necessary shall be performed whenever dredging conditions change in a manner affecting equipment calibration.
rows.normalized: Re-calibration shall be performed whenever dredging conditions change in a manner affecting equipment calibration.

rows.verbatim: Dredging sensory equipment shall be in good operating condition during dredging, and shall be mounted in plain sight of the dredge leverman.
rows.normalized: Dredging sensory equipment shall be in good operating condition and mounted in plain sight of the dredge leverman.

rows.normalized: Dredge leverman shall use required gauges, meters, and other sensory equipment to maximize dredge production.

rows.verbatim: h. The dredge shall be equipped with a degasser.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be equipped with a degasser.

rows.verbatim:
Attendant plant shall be composed of such fuel barges, derrick barges,
water barges, and other attendant or auxiliary plant as may be required
for operations under these specifications, whether or not items are
specifically mentioned.

rows.verbatim:
The attendant plant shall be in good condition
and of sufficient size and capacity to efficiently serve the dredge.
rows.normalized: The attendant plant must be in good condition and of sufficient size/capacity to efficiently serve the dredge.

rows.verbatim:
Fuel
barges and water barges shall comply with applicable US Coast Guard and US
Public Health Service Regulations.
rows.normalized: Fuel and water barges must comply with applicable US Coast Guard and US Public Health Service Regulations.

rows.verbatim:
All skiffs used on this contract shall
have a minimum hull length of 22 feet.
rows.normalized: All skiffs used on this contract must have a minimum hull length of 22 feet.

rows.normalized: The attendant plant must include at least two tenders per dredge for 24-hour operations.

of 35 feet, have twin screws, inboard, diesel powered engines with a

rows.verbatim:

times regardless of the pay status of the dredge.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall furnish, throughout the contract period, for the
exclusive use of the Government, one diesel or gasoline powered crew boat,

rows.normalized: The Contractor shall furnish a crew boat meeting specified speed, length, propeller, and passenger-capacity minimums for the Government's exclusive use throughout the contract period.

rows.verbatim:

exceed all applicable US Coast Guard regulations for vessels 65 feet or

rows.verbatim:
The crew boat shall be
equipped with the following:
(1) air conditioning and heating;
(2) VHF FM marine radio transceiver for ship to ship
communications, described in the paragraph entitled
"Communications Equipment";
(3) Navigation radar, as described in the paragraph entitled
"Navigation Radar";

paragraph entitled "Global Positioning System (GPS) Equipment".
rows.normalized: The crew boat shall be equipped with: (1) air conditioning/heating; (2) VHF FM marine radio; (3) navigation radar; (4) USCG Auxiliary/EM 385-1-1 compliant safety equipment; (5) GPS equipment.

rows.verbatim:
Equipment, which fails to perform because of insufficient power or other

The Contractor
shall make provisions to obtain a separate crew boat or vessel for
conducting Contractor-related operations.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall obtain a separate crew boat/vessel for its own Contractor-related operations.

rows.verbatim:
The minimum full time crew for
the crew boat shall be one operator.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall provide at least one full-time operator as minimum crew for the crew boat.

rows.verbatim:
The crew boat shall be operated and
available 24 hours a day.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall operate and make the crew boat available 24 hours a day.

rows.verbatim:
Smoking shall not be allowed inside the
cabin and operator's space while occupied by Government personnel.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall not allow smoking inside the cabin and operator's space while occupied by Government personnel.

rows.verbatim:
NO
SMOKING signs shall be posted.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall post NO SMOKING signs.

rows.verbatim:
The service of one or more towboats, in addition to the regularly assigned

paragraph entitled "Dredge Towing Service Item".
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall provide the service of one or more towboats, in addition to regularly assigned plant, for towing service as described.

rows.verbatim:
The towboat(s) shall
have horsepower to provide a minimum towing speed of three miles per hour
