capable of safely handling and moving the dredge and attendant plant in
currents of up to five miles per hour.
rows.normalized: The towboat(s) utilized shall be capable of safely handling and moving the dredge and attendant plant in currents up to five mph.

rows.verbatim:
The towboat shall have radio
equipment to communicate with other vessels in the vicinity of the dredge.
rows.normalized: The towboat shall have radio equipment to communicate with other vessels near the dredge.

rows.verbatim: All discharge pipeline shall be maintained in good condition.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain all discharge pipeline in good condition.

rows.verbatim: Leaks occurring in the pipeline shall be promptly stopped.
rows.normalized: Contractor must promptly stop leaks occurring in the pipeline.

rows.verbatim:
This shore
pipeline and associated equipment shall be considered as part of the
dredge attendant plant.
rows.normalized: Shore pipeline and associated equipment must be considered part of the dredge attendant plant.

rows.verbatim:
For floating pipeline equipment, the Contractor shall provide one
90 degree swivel elbow and one rigid elbow.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide one 90-degree swivel elbow and one rigid elbow for floating pipeline equipment.

rows.verbatim:
While in use, the
pipeline shall be secured at intervals not to exceed 400 feet.
rows.normalized: Contractor must secure the pipeline at intervals not exceeding 400 feet while in use.

rows.verbatim:
The
pipeline shall include two elbow pontoons (one each, right and left).
rows.normalized: The pipeline must include two elbow pontoons, one right and one left.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide adequate
numbers of anchors or skidder barges on the floating pipeline to

rows.normalized: Contractor must provide adequate anchors or skidder barges on floating pipeline to prevent separation due to river currents.

rows.verbatim:
Floating pipeline shall have navigation lights as specified

rows.normalized: Floating pipeline must have navigation lights as specified in Section 01 35 26.

rows.verbatim:
(e) Floating pipeline shall be placed to provide a minimum hazard to

When the submerged
pipeline is placed in shallow water, where the possibility exists for

The Contractor shall minimize use of heavy

rows.verbatim:
The equipment required to handle and
place shore pipeline shall be in good operating condition at all times

rows.verbatim:
The dredge, survey boat, and crew boat shall all be equipped with
SECTION 35 20 23.23 Page 17 navigation radar for use in inclement weather and at night.
rows.normalized: Dredge, survey boat, and crew boat must all be equipped with navigation radar for use in inclement weather and at night.

rows.verbatim:

equipment used under this contract shall be installed so that it will

a. The Contractor shall be required to furnish, on the request of the

rows.verbatim:

furnishes written justification, the Contracting Officer agrees in writing
to the substitution, and the following conditions are met:
a. The substitute dredge meets all of the requirements of this
contract and that the Contractor submits clear evidence that the
substitute dredge meets the plant requirements specified in the
paragraph entitled "Size and Equipment of Dredge Plant" and that the
substitute dredge performs at the rate set forth in the table located
in the applicable Dredging Region Section(s), on work similar to that
SECTION 35 20 23.23 Page 18 of this contract.
rows.normalized: If the Contractor wishes to substitute the dredge, it may do so only if it furnishes written justification, the Contracting Officer agrees in writing, and the substitute dredge meets all contract and plant requirements including performance rate; conditions listed, 1 of possibly more shown.

rows.verbatim:
The substitute dredge will be ready to begin
pumping material as soon as the original dredge is removed from
service.
b. The Government is reimbursed all costs in connection with
inspection of the substitute dredge, if such is required.
c. The substitute dredge is delivered to the worksite before the
original dredge is shut down and moved off the worksite. This
requirement does not apply to substitutions made during release
periods.
d. If the substitute dredge does not fit the same bid lot as the
original dredge, then rates for the substitute dredge will be computed
separately for the Dredging Payment Items as follows:
Substitute Dredge Hourly Rate =
(Original Base Item Estimated Quantity)x(Original Base Item Unit Price)
Estimated Quantity From Base Item Bid Schedule of Applicable Bid Lot
for Substitute Dredge
The remaining hours, if any, on the Basic Payment Items will be
prorated so that payments available to the Contractor under Option
Payment Items will be unchanged. Option dredging payment hours will
also be prorated separately, so that the total payments available to
the Contractor for exercised options remains unchanged.
e. Mobilization and demobilization costs for the substitute dredge
shall be borne by the Contractor.
f. Payment will resume for the substituting dredge:
(1) If the dredge returns to an assignment in the same dredging
region, when the cutterhead dredge material begins flowing out of
the discharge pipeline; or
(2) If the dredge returns to an assignment in a different dredging
region, when the cutterhead dredge material begins flowing out of
the discharge pipeline at the new assignment.

rows.verbatim: Disposal shall initiate at the western limit of proposed disposal.
rows.normalized: Contractor's disposal shall begin at the western limit of the proposed disposal area.

rows.verbatim: The discharge line shall be placed so as to direct the discharge parallel to the shoreline and in an easterly direction in an effort to maximize material retention.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall place the discharge line to direct discharge parallel to shoreline, easterly, to maximize retention.

rows.verbatim: The elevation of the material shall not exceed +5.0 feet MLG.
rows.normalized: Contractor's disposed material elevation shall not exceed +5.0 feet MLG.

rows.verbatim: As the maximum elevation is reached, the discharge line shall be moved as necessary to maintain construction of a continuous disposal berm, in compliance with this elevation.
rows.normalized: When the maximum elevation is reached, Contractor shall move the discharge line as needed to maintain a continuous berm within the elevation limit.

rows.verbatim: When disposing in the disposal area, the pipeline shall be routed from the Barataria Bar Channel to the disposal area across the gulf.
rows.normalized: When disposing, Contractor shall route the pipeline from the Barataria Bar Channel to the disposal area across the gulf.

rows.verbatim: No flotation excavation is allowed through the gulf.
rows.normalized: Contractor is prohibited from flotation excavation through the gulf.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall ensure that equipment and pipeline are not placed over the existing stone dike surrounding Fort Livingston.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure equipment and pipeline are not placed over the stone dike around Fort Livingston.

rows.verbatim: Fort Livingston is an archeological site that shall not be disturbed.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall not disturb the Fort Livingston archeological site.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide 21,000 feet of serviceable floating, submerged, or shore pipeline and all associated equipment as directed by the Government.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide 21,000 feet of serviceable pipeline and associated equipment as directed by the Government.

rows.verbatim: Before and after disposal surveys shall be taken at the Government's direction within the disposal area.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall take before/after disposal surveys within the disposal area as directed.

rows.verbatim: Cross-sections shall be taken normal to the beach, and spacing between the cross sections shall not exceed 100 feet.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall take cross-sections normal to the beach with spacing not exceeding 100 feet.

rows.verbatim: Soundings and/or rod readings shall be recorded to the nearest SECTION 35 20 23.23 19 Page 5 tenth of a foot and the distance between soundings and/or rod readings shall not exceed 25 feet.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall record soundings and/or rod readings to the nearest tenth of a foot, with distance between readings not exceeding 25 feet.

rows.verbatim: The surveys shall extend to adequately cover the area impacted by dredge material placement.
rows.normalized: Contractor's surveys shall adequately cover the area impacted by dredge material placement.

rows.verbatim: All surveys shall be tied/referenced to the centerline of the channel.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall reference all surveys to the channel centerline.

rows.verbatim: All notes resulting from these surveys shall be presented to the Contracting Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall present all survey notes to the COR.

rows.verbatim: The before and after disposal surveys shall be furnished to the Government in CAD and PDF formats including plan and section views.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall furnish before/after disposal surveys in CAD and PDF formats with plan and section views.

rows.verbatim: Survey data shall also be provided in ASCII XYZ format (easting, northing, elevation).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall also provide survey data in ASCII XYZ format.

rows.verbatim: All survey data shall be referenced to NAD83, State Plane Coordinates, LA South 1702 horizontally and Mean Low Gulf vertically.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall reference all survey data to NAD83 LA South 1702 horizontal and Mean Low Gulf vertical datums.

rows.verbatim: All disposal surveys shall be submitted and accepted before final payment is made to the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor's disposal surveys shall be submitted and accepted before final payment.

rows.verbatim: In addition, the before and after disposal surveys shall be submitted to Mr. Jeff Corbino electronically at Jeffrey.M.Corbino@usace.army.mil.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall also submit before/after disposal surveys electronically to Mr. Jeff Corbino.

rows.verbatim: In addition to the requirements in Section 35 01 50.73, paragraph entitled "Preliminary Field Surveys", controlled cross sections of the channel 500 feet in width or water's edge to water's edge, whichever one comes first, shall be taken at locations and intervals designated by the Contracting Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall take controlled cross sections (500 ft width or water's edge to water's edge) at COR-designated locations and intervals.

rows.verbatim: In addition to the requirements in Section 35 01 50.73, paragraph entitled "Before and After Dredging Cross Sections", the before and after dredging cross sections of the channel shall be taken at approximately 200-foot intervals along the channel.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall take before/after dredging cross sections at approximately 200-foot intervals.

rows.verbatim: In addition to the requirements in Section 35 01 50.73, paragraph entitled "Survey Data", the Contractor shall promptly plot the channel cross sections on a scale of 1 inch = 25 feet horizontal and 1 inch = 10 feet vertical.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall promptly plot channel cross sections at 1in=25ft horizontal and 1in=10ft vertical scale.

rows.verbatim: Nesting birds and their nests are protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act (MBTA) and must not be disturbed or destroyed.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not disturb or destroy protected nesting birds or their nests.

rows.verbatim: Protection within the project area shall be accomplished by the following: disturbance to deter nesting activity of coastal birds and wading birds prior to nesting; avoidance of active coastal bird, wading bird and pelican nesting areas; and avoidance of known eagle nests.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall accomplish bird protection via: pre-nesting disturbance/deterrence, avoidance of active nesting areas, and avoidance of known eagle nests.

rows.verbatim: Nest prevention and/or avoidance measures shall be required if nesting activity is observed during these times by the Contractor and verified by the Government.
rows.normalized: If nesting activity is observed and verified, Contractor shall implement nest prevention/avoidance measures.

rows.verbatim:
These indicators of breeding activity
shall be brought to the attention of the Government upon discovery to
determine if nest prevention measures or avoidance measures are required.
rows.normalized: Contractor must bring coastal bird breeding activity indicators to the Government's attention upon discovery.

rows.verbatim:
The presence of eagles on and near these nesting sites should
be reported to the Government and avoidance measures shall be implemented
upon discovery.
rows.normalized: Contractor must implement avoidance measures upon discovery of eagle nesting sites (reporting is recommended, not mandatory).

rows.verbatim:
In addition to the requirements in Section 01 57 20.00 10,
paragraph entitled "Implementation and Reporting", the Contractor
shall also submit the Bird Nesting Prevention Plan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must also submit the Bird Nesting Prevention Plan, in addition to Section 01 57 20.00 10 requirements.

rows.verbatim:
The presence of coastal birds, wading birds, pelicans, and/or
eagles exhibiting breeding behavior (as described in paragraph
entitled "General") within the minimum distances from the work area
(as specified in paragraph entitled "No Work Distances") shall be
immediately reported to the Administrative Contracting Officer and to
Jeff Corbino of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers at (504) 862-1958.
rows.normalized: Contractor must immediately report breeding behavior sightings within minimum distances to the Administrative Contracting Officer and Jeff Corbino.
No-work distance restrictions apply by species: coastal birds 650 ft, wading birds 1000 ft, pelicans 2000 ft, eagles 660 ft.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall prepare and submit, for approval, a plan detailing
the efforts that will be undertaken to prevent birds from nesting within
the minimum distances, as specified in the paragraph entitled "No Work
Distances", from any work activity.
rows.normalized: Contractor must prepare and submit for approval a bird nesting prevention plan.

rows.verbatim:
This plan
shall be submitted electronically to the Administrative Contracting
Officer, Contracting Officer's Representative, and to Mr. Jeff Corbino at
Jeffrey.M.Corbino@usace.army.mil.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit the nesting prevention plan electronically to the ACO, COR, and Mr. Jeff Corbino.

rows.verbatim:
Nest prevention measures shall be intended to deter birds from nesting on
the disposal area(s) and access corridor(s) without physically harming
birds during the nesting activity period.
rows.normalized: Nest prevention measures must deter nesting on disposal area(s)/access corridor(s) without harming birds.

rows.verbatim:
The use of any harassment measures
shall be in accordance with EM 385-1-1.
rows.normalized: Contractor's use of harassment measures must comply with EM 385-1-1.

rows.verbatim:
At minimum, nest prevention measures shall include the following:
Flagging/Streamers - Flagging and/or streamers at least two feet in
length and which consist of reflective plastic/mylar type material
shall be attached to the top of stakes at least three feet in height.
The stakes shall be driven into the ground at approximately 20-foot
intervals. Flagging and/or streamers shall be placed such that the
flags/streamers move in a light wind.

Vehicular/Pedestrian Traffic - At minimum, one terrain vehicle and/or
one person shall travel throughout the entire disposal area at least
once per hour from dawn to dusk.
rows.normalized: Nest prevention measures must at minimum include flagging/streamer requirements (length, material, stake height/spacing, placement) and vehicular/pedestrian patrol at least once per hour dawn to dusk.

rows.verbatim:
Upon the exercise of Option Item "Bird Nesting Prevention Measures", the
Contractor shall begin work within 24 hours.
rows.normalized: If Option Item "Bird Nesting Prevention Measures" is exercised, Contractor must begin work within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim:
Specific nest prevention
measures used during the work shall be monitored for effectiveness and may
require adjustment and/or modification.
rows.normalized: Contractor must monitor nest prevention measures for effectiveness.

rows.verbatim:
All equipment/supplies used for
nest prevention shall be removed from the work site upon the completion of
work and as directed by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove all nest-prevention equipment/supplies from the work site upon completion of work as directed by the CO.

rows.verbatim:
If bird nests are discovered at the work site, immediate notification
shall be made in accordance with paragraph entitled "Reporting".
rows.normalized: If bird nests are discovered at the work site, Contractor must immediately notify per the Reporting paragraph.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall immediately mark the perimeter or boundary of the bird
nesting area with flagging on stakes 3-feet above the ground surface and
no closer than 3 feet from the nearest nest.
rows.normalized: Contractor must immediately mark the bird nesting area perimeter with flagging on 3-ft stakes, no closer than 3 ft from the nest.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall then
immediately avoid the marked area and implement safe work distances from
the nest(s) as specified in paragraph entitled "No Work Distances", place
flagging to create exclusion zone(s) around the nest(s), and advise all
equipment operators of the bird nest(s) and exclusion zone(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor must immediately avoid the marked area, implement safe work distances, place flagging for exclusion zones, and advise equipment operators of nests/exclusion zones.

rows.verbatim: The following chart shows the minimum production rates the dredge must perform at as specified in Section 35 20 23.23, paragraph entitled "Required Production and Dredging Tolerances".
rows.normalized: The dredge must perform at the minimum production rates specified in Section 35 20 23.23, 'Required Production and Dredging Tolerances' (rates shown in accompanying chart).

rows.verbatim:

rows.normalized: Baratarira Bar Channel minimum production rate table, page 227, 3 rate entries by dredge size/pump configuration.

rows.verbatim:
If a dredge's submerged pump becomes inoperable and the Contractor
elects to continue dredging, then the Contractor will be allowed to
operate without the submerged pump provided the specifications have a bid
lot for that size dredge without a submerged pump and provided the dredge
meets the minimum production rate shown on the chart above and as
specified in Section 35 20 23.23, paragraph entitled "Required Production
and Dredging Tolerances".
rows.normalized: If a dredge's submerged pump becomes inoperable and Contractor elects to continue, Contractor may operate without the pump only if a bid lot exists for that dredge size without a pump and the dredge meets the minimum production rate.

rows.verbatim:
For a dredge with an inoperable submerged pump,
the new unit price per hour for "Barataria Bar Dredging" and "Barataria
Bar Option Dredging" shall be computed as follows:
New Unit Price Per Hour =
(Original Base Item Estimated Quantity)x(Original Base Item Unit Price)
Estimated Quantity From Base Item Bid Schedule of Applicable Bid Lot for
the Same Size Dredge Without a Submerged Pump
rows.normalized: For an inoperable-submerged-pump dredge, the new unit price per hour must be computed per the stated formula.

rows.verbatim:
The work under this contract requires use of the US Army Corps of
Engineers (USACE) National Dredging Quality Management Program (DQM) to
monitor the dredge's status at all times during the contract duration and
manage data history.
rows.normalized: Contractor's work requires use of the USACE DQM Program to monitor dredge status and manage data history throughout the contract.

rows.verbatim:
All costs in connection
therewith shall be considered a subsidiary obligation of the Contractor
and shall be included in the contract unit price per hour for the
applicable "Dredging" and "Option Dredging" items on the bidding schedule.
rows.normalized: Contractor must treat all DQM-related costs as a subsidiary obligation, included in the unit price per hour for Dredging/Option Dredging items.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall have a current certification from the DQM Program for
the cutter/suction head hydraulic dredge instrumentation system to be used
under this contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have a current DQM Program certification for the dredge instrumentation system used under the contract.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall have a digital copy of the Dredge Plant
Instrumentation Plan (DPIP) on file with the DQM Support Center.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep a digital copy of the DPIP on file with the DQM Support Center.

rows.verbatim:
While working on site, the Contractor
shall also maintain on the dredge a copy of the DPIP, which is easily
accessible to Government personnel at all times.
rows.normalized: While working on site, Contractor must maintain an accessible copy of the DPIP on the dredge.

rows.verbatim:
This document
shall accurately describe the sensors used, the configuration of the
system, how sensor data will be collected, how quality control on the
data will be performed, and how the
sensors/data-reporting equipment will be calibrated and repaired if it
fails.
rows.normalized: The DPIP document must accurately describe sensors used, system configuration, data collection, quality control, and calibration/repair processes.

rows.verbatim:
A description of the computed dredge-specific data and how the
sensor data will be transmitted to the DQM database shall also be
included.
rows.normalized: The DPIP must also include a description of computed dredge-specific data and sensor-data transmission to the DQM database.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to the start of work, the Contractor shall submit to the
DQM Support Center any addendum or modifications made to the plan
subsequent to its original submission.
rows.normalized: Prior to start of work, Contractor must submit any DPIP addenda/modifications to the DQM Support Center.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide, operate, and maintain all hardware and
software to meet these specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, operate, and maintain all hardware/software to meet these specifications.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall also be
responsible for the replacement, repair, and calibration of the sensors
and other necessary data acquisition equipment needed to supply the
required data.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for replacement, repair, and calibration of sensors and data acquisition equipment.

rows.verbatim:
The procedure to complete a repair shall be documented and completed as
soon as practical.
rows.normalized: The repair procedure must be documented and completed as soon as practical.

rows.verbatim:
If repair is not possible within two business days of any sensor failure,
a plan and timeline to complete the repair shall be submitted.
rows.normalized: If repair is not possible within two business days of a sensor failure, Contractor must submit a plan and timeline to complete the repair.

rows.verbatim:
Upon completion of a
repair, replacement, installation, modification, or calibration, the
Contractor shall notify the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR).
rows.normalized: Upon completion of any repair/replacement/installation/modification/calibration, Contractor must notify the COR.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall keep a log of sensor repair, replacement,
installation, modification, and calibration in the dredge's onboard copy
of the DPIP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep a log of sensor repair/replacement/installation/modification/calibration in the onboard DPIP.

rows.verbatim:
The log shall contain a three-year history of sensor
maintenance, including the time of the sensor failures (and subsequent
repairs), the time and results of sensor calibrations, the time of sensor
replacements, and the time that backup sensor systems were initiated to
provide the required data.
rows.normalized: The maintenance log must contain a three-year history including sensor failure/repair times, calibration times/results, replacement times, and backup-system initiation times.

rows.verbatim:
It shall also contain the name of the person responsible for the sensor
work.
rows.normalized: The maintenance log must also contain the name of the person responsible for the sensor work.

rows.verbatim:
Sensors installed shall be capable of collecting parameters within the
specified accuracies and resolutions indicated in the following
subparagraphs and transmit these parameters to the DQM database.
rows.normalized: Installed sensors must be capable of collecting parameters within specified accuracies/resolutions and transmitting them to the DQM database.

rows.verbatim:
All data
shall be transmitted in JSON message bundles.
rows.normalized: All data must be transmitted in JSON message bundles.

rows.verbatim:
Sensor data shall be transmitted as work event messages, and data which
relates to the operational state of the dredge or its sensors shall be
transmitted as state event messages.
rows.normalized: Sensor data must be transmitted as work event messages; operational-state data must be transmitted as state event messages.

rows.verbatim:
Every message bundle shall contain descriptive data that relates the
message to a given dredge plant and date/time.
rows.normalized: Every message bundle must contain descriptive data linking the message to a dredge plant and date/time.

rows.verbatim: The start of a message bundle shall be identified by the tag "DQM_data".
rows.normalized: The start of a message bundle must be identified by the tag "DQM_data".

rows.verbatim:
A message shall consist of an event type and its associated
data (as defined in paragraph entitled "Dredge Events"), a date/time stamp
indicating when the event occurred or started, and a comment providing
clarification or metadata about the situation.
rows.normalized: A message must consist of an event type/data, a date/time stamp, and a clarifying comment.

rows.verbatim:
The message time shall be
reported to the nearest second and referenced to Coordinated Universal
Time (UTC) time based on a 24-hour format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report message time to the nearest second in UTC, 24-hour format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).

rows.verbatim:
In order
to ensure accuracy and reliability, the time stamp shall be synchronized
to UTC format from an accurate, unchangeable source (for example, a GPS
National Marine Electronics Association [NMEA] datastring).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall synchronize the time stamp to UTC from an accurate, unchangeable source.

rows.verbatim:
Message time
shall be identified by the tag "msg_time".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify message time using the tag "msg_time".

rows.verbatim:
A comment shall be identified by the introductory tag
"comment", and the comment shall consist of no more than 250 characters.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall tag comments with "comment" and limit them to 250 characters.

rows.verbatim:
All work event
messages shall be initiated by the header tag "work_event".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall initiate all work event messages with header tag "work_event".

rows.verbatim:
Sensor values reported in a work event
shall represent a weighted average with the highest and lowest values not included in the calculated average
for the given interval.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report sensor values as a weighted average excluding the highest and lowest values.

rows.verbatim: The averaging routine used shall be consistent across all event triggers.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use a consistent averaging routine across all event triggers.

rows.verbatim:
This information shall be documented in the
DPIP sections that say "Calculations done external to the instrumentation".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall document averaging information in the DPIP sections referenced.

rows.verbatim:
The variation of the water level from the vertical datum for the river
stage or tidal gage described in the state events shall be obtained using
appropriate equipment to give the water level with an accuracy of +/- 0.1
ft.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall obtain water level variation from vertical datum with accuracy of +/- 0.1 ft.

rows.verbatim:
Vertical correction values above project datum described in the
dredging specification shall be entered with a positive sign and those
below with a negative sign.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall enter vertical correction values with positive/negative signs relative to datum.

rows.verbatim:
The tag for vertical correction shall be
"vert_correction".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use tag "vert_correction" for vertical correction.

rows.verbatim:
The X, Y, and Z components of the cutter/suction head location shall be
monitored.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall monitor X, Y, Z components of cutter/suction head location.

rows.verbatim:
The forwardmost point of the cutter/suction head shall be obtained using a
positioning system operating with a minimum accuracy level of 3-10 feet
horizontal Circular Error Probable (CEP).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall obtain forwardmost point of cutter/suction head using positioning system with minimum accuracy of 3-10 ft CEP.

rows.verbatim:
It shall be reported as
Latitude/Longitude WGS 84 in decimal degrees with West Longitude and South
Latitude values reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report position as Lat/Long WGS 84 decimal degrees, West/South as negative.

rows.verbatim:
Position values shall be identified
by the tags "ch_latitude" and "ch_longitude".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify position values with tags "ch_latitude" and "ch_longitude".

rows.verbatim:
Instrumentation shall be
capable of reporting to an accuracy of +/- 0.5 foot and a resolution to
the nearest 0.1 foot with no tidal adjustments.
rows.normalized: Contractor's instrumentation shall report cutter/suction invert depth to accuracy of +/-0.5 ft and resolution of 0.1 ft.

rows.verbatim:
The tag "ch_depth" shall be used to
identify the cutter/suction head depth.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use tag "ch_depth" to identify cutter/suction head depth.

rows.verbatim:
All
headings shall be provided using industry-standard equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide all headings using industry-standard equipment.

rows.verbatim:
The heading
shall be accurate to within 5 degrees and reported to the nearest whole
degree with values from 000 (true north) to 359 degrees referenced to a
clockwise positive direction convention.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report heading accurate to within 5 degrees, nearest whole degree, 000-359 clockwise convention.

rows.verbatim:
The tag "ch_heading" shall be
used to identify the cutter/suction head heading.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use tag "ch_heading" to identify cutter/suction head heading.

rows.verbatim:
Dredge activity
shall be monitored using a combination of the following parameters.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall monitor dredge activity using the following parameters.

rows.verbatim:
A flow-metering device, calibrated according to the manufacturer's
specifications, shall be used to record the slurry velocity to the nearest
0.01 fps with an accuracy of +/- 0.1 fps.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use a calibrated flow-metering device to record slurry velocity to nearest 0.01 fps, accuracy +/-0.1 fps.

rows.verbatim:
If the manufacturer does not
specify a frequency of recalibration, calibration shall be conducted prior
to the commencement of work.
rows.normalized: If manufacturer does not specify recalibration frequency, contractor shall calibrate the slurry velocity device before work begins.

rows.verbatim:
The slurry velocity shall be measured for the
same pipeline inside diameter as that used for the slurry density
measurement.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall measure slurry velocity using the same pipeline inside diameter as the slurry density measurement.

rows.verbatim: The tag "slurry_velocity" shall be associated with this value.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall associate tag "slurry_velocity" with slurry velocity value.

rows.verbatim:
A density-metering device, calibrated according to the manufacturer's
specifications, shall be used to record the slurry density of material
being moved to the nearest 0.01 g/cc.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use a calibrated density-metering device to record slurry density to nearest 0.01 g/cc.

rows.verbatim: The tag "slurry_density" shall be associated with this value.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall associate tag "slurry_density" with slurry density value.

rows.verbatim:
The shaft revolution rate (rev/min) shall be measured
with the highest level of accuracy that is standard on the vessel's
operational displays either at the bridge or in the engine room.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall measure pump shaft revolution rate at highest accuracy standard on vessel's operational displays.

rows.verbatim:
This value
shall be identified by the tag "rpm".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify pump RPM value with tag "rpm".

rows.verbatim:
Vacuum
pressure shall be identified by the tag "vacuum".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify vacuum pressure with tag "vacuum".

rows.verbatim:
The pump outlet pressure shall be measured in the discharge line on the
pump side of the flap valve in terms of pounds per square inch (psi) on a
gauge.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall measure pump outlet pressure in the discharge line in psi.

rows.verbatim: Pump outlet pressure shall be identified by the tag "outlet_psi".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify pump outlet pressure with tag "outlet_psi".

rows.verbatim:
The X and Y position of the terminal end of the outfall pipe shall be
monitored continuously and the position reported as part of the work event
string.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall continuously monitor outfall pipe X/Y position and report as part of the work event string.

rows.verbatim:
The horizontal position of the outfall end of the discharge pipe shall be
obtained using a positioning system operating with a minimum accuracy
level of 3-10 feet horizontal Circular Error Probable (CEP).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall obtain discharge pipe outfall horizontal position with minimum accuracy of 3-10 ft CEP.

rows.verbatim:
It shall be
reported as Latitude/Longitude WGS 84 in decimal degrees with West
Longitude and South Latitude values being reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report discharge outfall position as Lat/Long WGS 84 decimal degrees, West/South as negative.

rows.verbatim:
Position
values shall be identified by the tags "outfall_latitude" and
"outfall_longitude".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify position values with tags "outfall_latitude" and "outfall_longitude".

rows.verbatim:
Each type of state event message shall be indicated by a
specific header tag as enumerated in the following subparagraphs.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall indicate each state event message type with a specific header tag per the enumerated subparagraphs.

rows.verbatim:
The
leverman's time shall be entered to the nearest second as local time and
automatically converted to and reported in UTC based on a 24-hour format
(YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall enter leverman's time to the nearest second, convert to and report in UTC 24-hour format.

rows.verbatim:
Message time shall be identified by the tag
"msg_time".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify state event message time with tag "msg_time".

rows.verbatim:
Information concerning the contract under which dredging is being
performed shall be reported at the start and completion of each contract
using the header tag "contract_event".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report contract information at start and completion of each contract using tag "contract_event".

rows.verbatim:
The USACE-assigned contract number for the project shall be reported using
the tag "contract_number".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report USACE-assigned contract number using tag "contract_number".

rows.verbatim:
The start and end of a contract
shall be reported using the tag "event_type" with the appropriate value of
"start" or "end".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report contract start/end using tag "event_type" with value "start" or "end".

rows.verbatim:
Properties associated with the vertical correction (see paragraph entitled
"Vertical Correction") for the tide station/river stage gage shall be
grouped together under the header tag "station_event".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall group tide station/river gage vertical correction properties under tag "station_event".

rows.verbatim:
This information
shall be sent at the start of the contract and each time the dredge has
moved enough to change the station being used.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall send station event information at contract start and each time the station changes.

rows.verbatim: It shall be introduced by the tag "station_name", and it shall consist of a descriptor of no more than 25 characters.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall tag station name "station_name" and limit it to 25 characters.

rows.verbatim:
The leverman's estimate of the length of pipe downflow from the dredge
pump, measured to the nearest whole foot, shall be reported under the
header tag "pipe_length_event".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report leverman's estimate of pipe length, to the nearest whole foot, under tag "pipe_length_event".

rows.verbatim:
This information shall be sent at the
start of the contract and at the completion of each 24-hour period ending
at midnight local time.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall send pipe length information at contract start and completion of each 24-hour period ending at midnight local time.

rows.verbatim:
The total length of floating pipe shall be reported with the tag
"length_floating".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report total floating pipe length with tag "length_floating".

rows.verbatim:
The total length of submerged pipe shall be reported with the tag
"length_submerged".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report total submerged pipe length with tag "length_submerged".

rows.verbatim:
The total length of shore pipe shall be reported with the tag
"length_land".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report total shore pipe length with tag "length_land".

rows.verbatim:
Information concerning the booster pumps being used shall be included
under the header tag "booster_pump_event".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report booster pump information under tag "booster_pump_event".

rows.verbatim: A message shall be sent to indicate any change in the status of the booster pumps being used.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall send a message indicating any change in booster pump status.

rows.verbatim:
Upon the addition or removal of a booster pump, the total number of
booster pumps being used shall be reported with the tag "booster_total".
rows.normalized: Upon addition or removal of a booster pump, contractor shall report total number of booster pumps with tag "booster_total".

rows.verbatim:
The dredge advance, the total forward progress of the dredge relative to
the centerline of the cut, shall be measured to the nearest whole foot and
cumulatively calculated over a 24-hour period from midnight to midnight
local time.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall measure dredge advance to nearest whole foot, cumulatively over 24-hour period midnight to midnight.

rows.verbatim: It shall be identified by the tag "advance_daily".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify dredge advance with tag "advance_daily".

rows.verbatim:
The msg_time associated with this tag shall be reported as the first timestamp
of the following 24-hour period (based on the local time) rather than as
midnight of the day for which the value was calculated, and it shall be
reported in Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report msg_time for dredge advance as first timestamp of the following 24-hour period, in GMT.

rows.verbatim:
The X and Y position of the terminal end of the outfall pipe shall be
monitored and sent at the start of the contract and thereafter according
to the following table.
rows.normalized: Outfall position reporting-frequency table, page 239, 4 discharge-location rows (Open Water, Scow, Beach, Upland) x 3 columns.

rows.verbatim:
Discharge Heading and Pipe Elevation may be omitted if the dredge is not
discharging into an upland disposal site.
rows.normalized: Contractor may omit Discharge Heading and Pipe Elevation if not discharging into an upland disposal site.

rows.verbatim:
For
beach nourishment, the horizontal X and Y position of the outfall shall be
sent at the start of the contract and at the completion of each 24-hour
period ending at midnight local time.
rows.normalized: For beach nourishment, contractor shall send outfall X/Y position at contract start and end of each 24-hour period ending midnight local time.

rows.verbatim:
Information on where the slurry is being discharged shall be reported with
the tag "outfall_location".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report discharge location with tag "outfall_location".

rows.verbatim:
Acceptable values include "upland", "open
water", "beach", and "scow".
rows.normalized: Contractor's discharge location values are limited to "upland", "open water", "beach", and "scow"; 4 values in total.

rows.verbatim:
The horizontal position of the outfall end of the discharge pipe shall be
obtained using a positioning system operating with a minimum accuracy
level of 3-10 feet horizontal Circular Error Probable (CEP).
rows.normalized: Contractor shall obtain discharge pipe outfall horizontal position with minimum accuracy of 3-10 ft CEP (state event reporting).

rows.verbatim:
It shall be
reported as Latitude/Longitude WGS 84 in decimal degrees with West
Longitude and South Latitude values being reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report discharge outfall position as Lat/Long WGS 84 decimal degrees, West/South negative (state event).

rows.verbatim:
Position
values shall be identified by the tags "outfall_latitude" and
"outfall_longitude".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify outfall position values with tags "outfall_latitude" and "outfall_longitude" (state event).

rows.verbatim:
All
headings shall be provided using industry-standard equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide discharge outfall heading using industry-standard equipment.

rows.verbatim:
They shall
be accurate to within 5 degrees and reported to the nearest whole degree
with values from 000 (true north) to 359 degrees referenced to a clockwise
positive direction convention.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report discharge outfall heading accurate to within 5 degrees, nearest whole degree, 000-359 clockwise.

rows.verbatim:
The discharge heading shall be identified
by the tag "outfall_heading".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall identify discharge heading with tag "outfall_heading".

rows.verbatim:
The tag "outfall_elevation"
shall be used to identify this elevation.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use tag "outfall_elevation" to identify discharge pipe elevation.

rows.verbatim:
Delays and dredge downtime shall be reported at the conclusion of the
event.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report delays and dredge downtime at the conclusion of the event.

rows.verbatim:
The reason for the non-effective work time shall be submitted under
the header tag "non_eff_event" within 24 hours of the event.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit reason for non-effective work time under tag "non_eff_event" within 24 hours of the event.

rows.verbatim:
The start and end times for the non-effective work event shall be reported
using the tags "msg_start_time" and "msg_end_time".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall report start/end times of non-effective work event using tags "msg_start_time" and "msg_end_time".

rows.verbatim:
The dredge operator indication of production delays, as listed on Form
4267, shall be transmitted at the end of the non-effective interval.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall transmit dredge function code (per Form 4267) at the end of the non-effective interval.

rows.verbatim:
Dredge function event messages shall be identified by the tag
"function_code" and shall consist of one of the following standardized
entries to indicate the operation:
AGV Assisting Grounded Vessels
CCH Change Cutterhead
CCSH Clear Cutter Suction
CLPJ Change Location Bar
COLL Collision
CPPL Clear Pump Pipeline
CPR Change Impeller
DR Dike Repair
FBD Fire Boat Drills
HPL Handling Pipe Line
HSL Handling Swing Line
HSP Handling Shore Pipe
LDNE Loss Due to Natural Elements
LDPV Loss Due to Passing Vessel
LNL Transfer to New Location
MISC Miscellaneous
MOB Mobilization & Demobilization
MSC Miscellaneous/Non-pay
OC Out of Commission
OR Operating Repairs
P Preparation
PREP Preparation & Making Up Tow
RPL Repair Pipeline
SB Sounding & Buoying
SBT Stand-By Time as Directed
SH Sundays-Holidays
TFS Taking on Fuel & Supplies
TOW Time on Tow
WAP Waiting Attendant Plant
rows.normalized: Contractor shall tag dredge function event messages "function_code" using one of the standardized entries; 30 codes in total.

rows.verbatim: The "comment" tag shall be used to provide additional explanation for the noted delays or downtimes.
rows.normalized: Contractor's system shall use the 'comment' tag to explain noted delays or downtimes.

rows.verbatim:
For example, when the code "LDPV" (Loss Due to Passing Vessel) is indicated, the name of the vessel and the number of
tows shall be listed with the "comment" tag.
rows.normalized: When code LDPV is indicated, vessel name and number of tows shall be listed with the comment tag.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor's DQM system shall be capable of collecting and
transmitting data to the DQM system.
rows.normalized: Contractor's DQM system shall be capable of collecting and transmitting data to the DQM system.

rows.verbatim:
The applicable parameters from paragraph entitled "Requirements for Reported Data" shall be recorded as
events locally and continuously transmitted to the DQM database anytime an
Internet connection is available.
rows.normalized: Applicable parameters shall be recorded as events locally and continuously transmitted to the DQM database whenever Internet connection is available.

rows.verbatim:
The computer system shall be a standalone system, exclusive to the DQM monitoring
system, and shall have USACE DQM software installed on it.
rows.normalized: The DQM computer system shall be a standalone system exclusive to DQM monitoring and shall have USACE DQM software installed.

rows.verbatim:
If a hardware
problem occurs, or if a part of the system is physically damaged, then the
Contractor shall be responsible for repairing it within two business days
of the determination of the condition or submitting a plan and timeline
for repair if the repair will take more than two business days.
rows.normalized: If a hardware problem occurs or a part is damaged, Contractor shall repair within two business days or submit a repair plan/timeline if repair exceeds two business days.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall provide a dedicated onboard computer for use by the
Dredging Quality Management system.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide a dedicated onboard computer for the DQM system.

rows.verbatim: This computer shall run the USACE DQM software and receive data from the Contractor's data-reporting interface.
rows.normalized: The onboard computer shall run USACE DQM software and receive data from the Contractor's data-reporting interface.

rows.verbatim:
This computer must meet or exceed the following performance specifications:
CPU Intel or AMD processor with a (non-overclocked) clock
speed of at least 1.6 gigahertz (GHz)
Hard drive 250 gigabytes (GB); internal
RAM 4 gigabytes (GB)
Ethernet adapter Internal network card with a RJ-45 connector
Ports 1 free serial port with standard 9-pin connectors; 1
free USB port
Other hardware Keyboard, mouse, monitor
rows.normalized: Computer hardware specification table (CPU, hard drive, RAM, ethernet, ports, other hardware), page 241, 6 specification items.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall install a fully licensed copy of Windows 10
Professional Operating System or later on the computer specified above.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall install a fully licensed copy of Windows 10 Professional or later on the specified computer.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall also install any necessary manufacturer-provided
drivers for the installed hardware.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall install any necessary manufacturer-provided drivers for installed hardware.

rows.verbatim:
No other software which conflicts with this function
shall be installed on it.
rows.normalized: No conflicting software shall be installed on the DQM computer.

rows.verbatim:
The DQM computer shall also have the
USACE-provided Dredging Quality Management Onboard Software (DQMOBS)
installed on it by DQM personnel.
rows.normalized: The DQM computer shall have USACE-provided DQMOBS software installed on it by DQM personnel.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall supply an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) for the
computer and networking equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall supply a UPS for the computer and networking equipment.

rows.verbatim:
It shall interface with the DQM
computer to communicate UPS status, and it shall provide backup power at 1
kVA for a minimum of 10 minutes.
rows.normalized: The UPS shall interface with the DQM computer to communicate status and shall provide backup power at 1 kVA for at least 10 minutes.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure that
sufficient power outlets are available to run all specified equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall ensure sufficient power outlets are available to run all specified equipment.

rows.verbatim: A web service shall be used to report sensor data to the DQM database.
rows.normalized: A web service shall be used to report sensor data to the DQM database.

rows.verbatim:
Data
shall be transmitted as it is collected in real time and pushed to
the DQM web service.
rows.normalized: Data shall be transmitted in real time and pushed to the DQM web service.

rows.verbatim:
If the web service is not available or returns an
error message, the data shall be stored in a queue and transmitted upon
re-establishment of the connection, starting with the oldest data in the
queue and continuing until real-time transmission is restored.
rows.normalized: If the web service is unavailable or errors, data shall be queued and transmitted upon reconnection, oldest first, until real-time transmission is restored.

rows.verbatim:
Contact dqm-support@usace.army.mil to obtain the web service URL and the
appropriate key credentials and communication protocol.
rows.normalized: Contact DQM support to obtain the web service URL, key credentials, and communication protocol.

rows.verbatim:
If this option is chosen, a display of the raw data being transmitted to
DQM must be easily accessible and visible onboard the dredge.
rows.normalized: If Option 2 is chosen, a display of raw data transmitted to DQM must be easily accessible and visible onboard the dredge.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall maintain an Internet connection capable of
transmitting real-time data to the DQM server as well as enough additional
bandwidth to clear historically queued data when a connection is
re-established.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain an Internet connection capable of real-time DQM data transmission plus bandwidth to clear queued data upon reconnection.

rows.verbatim:
The telemetry system shall always be available and have
connectivity in the contract area.
rows.normalized: The telemetry system shall always be available and have connectivity in the contract area.

rows.verbatim:
If connectivity is lost, unsent data
shall be queued and transmitted upon restoration of connectivity.
rows.normalized: If connectivity is lost, unsent data shall be queued and transmitted upon restoration of connectivity.

rows.verbatim:
Delays
in pushing real-time data to the DQM database should not exceed four
hours.
rows.normalized: Delays in pushing real-time data to the DQM database should not exceed four hours.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall acquire and install all necessary hardware and
software to make the Internet connection available for data transmission
to the DQM web service.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall acquire and install all necessary hardware and software to enable Internet connection for DQM web service data transmission.

rows.verbatim:
The hardware and software shall be configured to
allow the DQM Support Center remote access to this computer, and the
telemetry system shall be capable of meeting these minimum reporting
requirements in all operating conditions.
rows.normalized: Hardware/software shall be configured to allow DQM Support Center remote access, and telemetry system shall meet minimum reporting requirements in all operating conditions.

rows.verbatim:
Portions of this Contractor-collected information, as described in this specification,
shall be routed to the DQM computer on a real-time basis, utilizing one of
the options outlined in paragraphs 3.2.1 "Option 1: Computer Requirements"
through 3.2.5 "Internet Access".
rows.normalized: Portions of Contractor-collected information shall be routed to the DQM computer in real time using one of the specified options.

rows.verbatim:
If the serial transmission option is
used, sensor data shall be sent to the DQM computer via an RS-232 serial
interface with a baud rate of 9600 or 19200 bps.
rows.normalized: If the serial transmission option is used, sensor data shall be sent to the DQM computer via RS-232 at 9600 or 19200 bps.

rows.verbatim:
The serial interface
shall be configured as 8 bits, no parity, and no flow control.
rows.normalized: The serial interface shall be configured as 8 bits, no parity, no flow control.

rows.verbatim:
Information regarding changes in the state of the dredge
shall be digitally logged and transmitted as close to the time of the
occurrence as possible.
rows.normalized: Information regarding changes in dredge state shall be digitally logged and transmitted as close to occurrence as possible.

rows.verbatim:
Portions of this Contractor-collected
information, as described in this specification, and calculations based on
them shall be stored and transmitted to the DQM database on a near
real-time basis.
rows.normalized: Portions of Contractor-collected information and calculations shall be stored and transmitted to the DQM database on a near real-time basis.

rows.verbatim:
Additionally,
information regarding the state of the dredge shall be digitally logged and
transmitted.
rows.normalized: Information regarding the state of the dredge shall be digitally logged and transmitted.

rows.verbatim: Data shall be logged as a series of events.
rows.normalized: Data shall be logged as a series of events.

rows.verbatim:
Each event shall consist of a
dataset containing dredge information (as defined in paragraph entitled
"Requirements for Reported Data").
rows.normalized: Each event shall consist of a dataset containing dredge information as defined.

rows.verbatim:
Each set of measurements (for example,
time and position) shall be considered an event, and there shall be a 6-12
second interval between work events.
rows.normalized: Each set of measurements shall be considered an event, with a 6-12 second interval between work events.

rows.verbatim:
This interval
shall remain consistent across event types for the dredge plant.
rows.normalized: The interval between work events shall remain consistent across event types for the dredge plant.

rows.verbatim:
A standard data string shall be recorded within one second of an event
trigger with the time stamp and all parameters reflecting when the event
happened.
rows.normalized: A standard data string shall be recorded within one second of an event trigger with timestamp and parameters.

rows.verbatim:
A set of descriptive information (event name, time, description, comment)
shall be considered a state event.
rows.normalized: A set of descriptive information shall be considered a state event.

rows.verbatim:
These events shall be recorded within
24 hours of a change in state with the time stamp reflecting when the
event happened.
rows.normalized: State events shall be recorded within 24 hours of a change in state with a timestamp reflecting when it happened.

rows.verbatim:
The data shall be formatted as JSON (JavaScript Object Notation, as
defined at http://www.json.org) strings of arbitrary length.
rows.normalized: Data shall be formatted as JSON strings of arbitrary length.

rows.verbatim:
No "Null" value
strings shall be included in a message bundle.
rows.normalized: No 'Null' value strings shall be included in a message bundle.

rows.verbatim:
Message bundle
****************************
{
"DQM_Data": {
"plant_identifier": <integer value 0000-9999>,
"transmission_time": <24-hour UTC time YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS>,
"messages": [
rows.normalized: JSON message bundle field-definition table/schema for DQM data transmission, pages 244-245, approximately 8 message types with ~40 fields total.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall maintain an archive of all data sent to the DQM
computer during the dredging contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall maintain an archive of all data sent to the DQM computer during the dredging contract.

rows.verbatim:
The COR may require, at no increase
in the contract price, that the Contractor provide a copy of these data
covering specified time periods.
rows.normalized: If the COR requires it, Contractor shall provide a copy of data covering specified time periods at no additional cost.

rows.verbatim:
The data shall be provided in the same JSON format as would have been
transmitted to the DQM computer.
rows.normalized: Requested archive data shall be provided in the same JSON format as would have been transmitted to the DQM computer.

rows.verbatim:
There
shall be no line breaks between the parameters, and each record string
shall be on separate line.
rows.normalized: There shall be no line breaks between parameters, and each record string shall be on a separate line.

rows.verbatim:
The naming convention for the files shall be <
dredgename>_<StartYYYYMMddhhmmss>_<EndYYYYMMddhhmmss>.txt.
rows.normalized: The naming convention for archive files shall be <dredgename>_<StartYYYYMMddhhmmss>_<EndYYYYMMddhhmmss>.txt.

rows.verbatim: Data submission shall be via a storage medium acceptable to the COR.
rows.normalized: Data submission shall be via a storage medium acceptable to the COR.

rows.verbatim:
At the end of the dredging contact, the Contractor shall call the DQM
Support Center prior to discarding the data.
rows.normalized: At the end of the dredging contract, Contractor shall call the DQM Support Center prior to discarding data.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor's National Dredging Quality Management Program's data
transmission shall be fully operational at the start of dredging
operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor's DQM data transmission shall be fully operational at the start of dredging operations.

rows.verbatim:
To meet contract requirements for operability, the
Contractor's system shall provide an accurate data string return and be
compliant with hardware requirements.
rows.normalized: Contractor's system shall provide accurate data string return and be compliant with hardware requirements to meet operability requirements.

rows.verbatim:
Repairs necessary
to restore data return compliance shall be made within two business days,
or a plan and timeline for repair shall be submitted to the DQM Data
Acquisition and Analysis Team if the repair will take more than two
business days.
rows.normalized: Repairs to restore data compliance shall be made within two business days, or a repair plan/timeline shall be submitted if repair exceeds two business days.

rows.verbatim:
Failure by the Contractor to report quality data within the
specified time window for dredge measurements as stated in the
specifications (see paragraphs entitled "Internet Access", "Data
Measurement Frequency" and "Parameter Transmission to the Web Service")
will result in withholding of up to 10% of the contract progress payment
per clause 52.232-5.
rows.normalized: Failure by the Contractor to report quality data within the specified time window will result in withholding of up to 10% of the contract progress payment.

DPIP https://dqm.usace.army.mil
DQM System Paragraph entitled "National Dredging Quality Management
Program System Requirements"
